#788. See Prince George's Winning Reunion With Dad Prince William

Prince George reunited with his dad Prince William to watch a soccer game in Spain during his break from boarding school at Eton College in Barcelona on Nov. 3.

Prince George is having a ball on his school break.

Less than two months after the 13-year-old son of Prince William and Kate Middleton began boarding school at Eton College, he reunited with his dad to watch Aston Villa FC face off against FC Barcelona in Barcelona, Spain, on Nov. 3.

Though William—also dad to kids Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, 8, with Kate—is a longtime supporter of Aston Villa, Barcelona sent a royally sweet message to the duo.

“FC Barcelona is honoured to welcome His Royal Highness The Prince of Wales and His Royal Highness Prince George to the Spotify Camp Nou,” the Spanish soccer team wrote on X Nov. 3. “Thank you for joining us for a special evening of Champions League football featuring your beloved Aston Villa.”

And for their father-son field day, William, 44, and George teamed up for matching casual dark-colored outfits, bundling up against the cold. While William donned a black jacket and simple black cap, his son wore a black and white striped Aston Villa windbreaker.

Although the Birmingham team lost to Barcelona, William and George’s reunion was still pitch perfect. After all, the pair were locked in on the match, with the teen even sweetly leaning his head on his dad’s shoulder at one point.

The outing comes amid George’s break from school at Eton College, according to the institution’s website.

And as he spends some quality with his dad before he returns to school in a few days, George’s mom previously shared she was looking forward to seeing her eldest son during his time off.

While visiting a charity shop on Oct. 22, Kate expressed her excitement about seeing her kids on their half-term break, telling a young child, per Hello! magazine, “My children break up tomorrow and I can't wait to have them all home.”

It’s been nearly two months since the Princess of Wales dropped off George at Eton College—William and Prince Harry’s alma mater—on Sept. 8.

At the time, George looked royally ready for his new chapter, matching his dad in a dark blue suit and tie.

As his parents prepared to send their son off, William and Kate, 44, shook hands with the headmaster, per videos shared online, with the school officially telling George, “Welcome, good luck and enjoy.”

For a closer look at the royal family’s adventures this year, keep reading…

The Wales family's team of five consisting of Prince William, Kate Middleton, Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis attended the August 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

As a cancer survivor, the Princess of Wales took part in the National Three Peaks Challenge—climbing the three highest peaks in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours in June 2026—to support The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity. And her loved ones were there to show their support.

Per tradition, William, Kate and their kids joined royal family members in closing out the June 2026 Trooping the Colour ceremonial parade with a wave from the balcony of London's Buckingham Palace.

The Wales family hopped over to St. George's Chapel at Windsor Castle to celebrate Easter in April 2026.

Coordinating in navy and green attire, William, Kate, George, Charlotte and Louis got into the holiday spirit by attending the December 2025 Together at Christmas Carol Service at London's Westminster Abbey.

The couple and their two eldest children served up another sweet family moment at Wimbledon in July 2025.

Louis was captivated by the flypast he watched with his mom, dad and siblings from Buckingham Palace's balcony that took place on the 80th anniversary of VE Day in May 2025.

From singing "King of My Heart" to meeting the future kings of England! Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce snapped a selfie with William, George and Charlotte during one of her June 2024 London shows.

Fast-forward two years later, and William appeared on Travis' podcast New Heights, with the episode dropping the same day the Kansas City Chiefs tight end wed the Grammy winner in July 2026.

For Father's Day 2024, Kate shared this snap of William and their kids enjoying a day at the beach.

"We love you, Papa," the June 2024 post read, "Happy Father’s Day G, C & L."

A then 5-year-old Louis sweetly stole the show during Trooping the Colour 2023.

It's Beginning to Look A Lot Like Christmas

The Wales family shared jolly smiles as they headed to Christmas service at Sandringham's St. Mary Magdalene Church in 2023.

George enjoyed a slice of pizza while attending a London cricket match with his dad in July 2023.

Louis, George and Charlotte rode off to London's Westminster Abbey for their grandfather King Charles III's coronation ceremony in May 2023—though the monarch immediately acceded to the throne following the death of his mother Queen Elizabeth II in September 2022.

As part of the coronation activities, William and Kate reminded their kids of the importance of service by bringing all three of them to volunteer at the Big Help Out in May 2023.

Kicking off another year, William and Kate walked George, Charlotte and Louis to their "settling in" day at their primary school in the Berkshire countryside in September 2022.

Charlotte gave her dad a thumbs-up as they attended the Commonwealth Games' swimming event with Kate in August 2022.

While celebrating the Platinum Jubilee of Queen Elizabeth II in June 2022, Louis sweetly wrapped his arm around his mom.

He also joined his older siblings in a carriage ride to mark the momentous occasion.

As William, Kate, George and Charlotte headed to 2022's Easter service at St. George's Chapel in Windsor, fans might have noticed some bunny was missing. However, the service may have been too long for Louis, who was only 4 years old at the time and already proving he could get into some adorable mischief.

The family of five attended a performance of Pantoland at London's Palladium Theatre in December 2020.

Making his Trooping the Colour balcony debut nearly two months after his first birthday, Louis gave a little wave alongside his parents and siblings at the June 2019 event.

Joined by Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, King Charles III and Queen Camilla and the Middletons, William held the hands of then-3-year-old Charlotte and almost 5-year-old George as they walked into Chapel Royal at St James's Palace for the July 2018 christening of Louis.

Completing William and Kate's family of five, Prince Louis Arthur Charles was born at St. Mary's Hospital in London, the same place as his older siblings, on April 23, 2018.

Charlotte and Kate twinned in pink while attending Trooping the Colour 2017.

After Princess Charlotte Elizabeth Diana was born on May 2, 2015, William brought George over to the hospital to meet his sister.

William and Kate became parents for the first time when they welcomed Prince George Alexander Louis on July 22, 2013.

#787. Rangers' McInnes eager for Penrice deal

Penrice set up the only goal in Rangers' Premier Sports Cup semi-final win over Aberdeen

It's been a very good few days for James Penrice, with a first Scotland call-up following on from a first senior semi-final victory, so it is little wonder manager Derek McInnes is so keen to keep him at Rangers.

The 27-year-old started like a train at Ibrox and has just kept going.

A day after signing on loan from AEK Athens, in his first outing of the season, the left-back turned in a player-of-the-match display, scoring and providing an assist in the 5-1 demolition of St Mirren.

It was Rangers' first win of the campaign after Europa League elimination and a tally of one point from their opening two games in the Scottish Premiership.

McInnes' side have not lost a domestic match since, stretching that run to 12 on Saturday as Penrice set up the only goal against Aberdeen at Hampden.

With his low shot turned home by Ryan Naderi, Rangers go into December's League Cup final against Hibernian looking for their first silverware since 2023. Penrice will hope to add to an unlikely medal set of Scottish League One and the Greek Super League.

AEK Athens paid Â£2m for the former Partick Thistle and Livingston defender in July 2025 after one stand-out year with Heart of Midlothian.

In Greece, he played 32 times for the side who secured their 14th national title. Sixteen of those appearances were starts as he alternated with Albania international Stavros Pilios.

The loan to Rangers includes an option to buy and reports from Athens suggest AEK would like to renegotiate given the impact Penrice has made.

Other reports have the fee agreed over the summer at a combined Â£1.2m, which looks like a steal.

"I've made my feelings clear on it," McInnes said. "Ideally, we'd like to have done it on a permanent, but the best way forward at the time was a loan.

"I think we are all aware of what it needs to be to make it permanent, but I think there is a lot of goodwill all round and that is something we would like to do."

McInnes on cup final carrot, Penrice future & Paisley trip

Is inexperience counting against youthful Rangers?

Penrice 'incredibly proud' of first Scotland call-up

McInnes sprang a surprise on Celtic by using Penrice in midfield for their League Cup meeting at Ibrox. The tactic worked a treat as Rangers romped to a 3-0 win.

He snuffed out the threat of Benjamin Nygren and moved wide in transition to great effect as the visitors were overwhelmed.

The same starting XI earned a 1-0 victory at Celtic Park a week later.

"What he's done since the first minute is just play with so much enthusiasm," McInnes said.

"He brings quality and energy. The fans take to him because of how he performs and how much he wants to win.

"He's a player that I trust and the supporters trust, so hopefully we can make it a longer-term thing."

A relatively late bloomer, Penrice spoke of his pride and a "weird feeling" to RangersTV after being named in the Scotland squad for this month's Nations League double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

"I didn't ever think going through the early part of my career, I would ever be called up," he said.

McInnes shared his delight in the recognition while stressing it comes as "no real surprise" given current form. Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli echoed those thoughts, describing the selection as "logical".

Scotland skipper Andy Robertson will overtake Sir Kenny Dalglish's record of 102 caps if he plays in both games, so an uncapped left-back might have to be patient.

Then we have Kieran Tierney on 58 caps and Josh Doig embarking on his fourth Serie A campaign, so competition in that area is stiff.

"James deserves it and hopefully he can get on the pitch and come back with a couple of caps," McInnes added.

"The thing that screams out of James is hunger. He's driven himself to get to where he is now. He plays with hunger and he trains with hunger.

"I don't think anybody should ever underestimate working with hungry players.

"As soon as you become too comfortable, you become complacent, for me. And I think that there is a real hunger there to establish himself here. He wants to be here."

#785. Wilson returns as Wales call up uncapped Duncan

Joe Duncan (left) has won two caps for Wales Under-21s, while Harry Wilson has 69 senior caps

Harry Wilson is back in Wales' squad for their Nations League matches against Norway and Portugal, while there is a first call-up for young goalkeeper Joe Duncan.

Wilson has been one of Wales' most influential players in recent years but injuries mean the Leeds United attacking midfielder has not featured for his country since March.

His Leeds team-mate, centre-back Joe Rodon, also returns despite not playing since injuring his hamstring in August.

"We've clearly seen in my time here the influence Harry's had," said Wales head coach Craig Bellamy. "He's had a big influence on the team. He's been outstanding for us.

"Joe's been immense, so it's great having him. Players have to come through [for their clubs] this week so, fingers crossed when we report Sunday, we have these players available because they're really important for us."

Cardiff City playmaker Rubin Colwill is recalled but fellow midfielder Jordan James is out after sustaining an injury while playing for Wolves against the Bluebirds last Saturday.

The only new call-up is 20-year-old Duncan, who is on loan at National League side Southend United from Championship outfit Bristol City, as Bellamy looks to freshen up Wales' ageing crop of keepers.

Born in Bristol but qualifying for Wales through his maternal grandfather from Cardiff, Duncan has represented Wales Under-21s and replaces Everton back-up Tom King in the senior squad.

Wales have a shortage of goalkeeping options, with a noticeable lack of young players emerging. First-team regulars Karl Darlow and Danny Ward are 36 and 33 respectively, while King is 31.

"It's a clear issue at this moment, of course it is, because of the age of our goalkeepers," said Bellamy.

"At one stage a long time ago, we had the world's number one goalkeeper [Neville Southall], most incredible goalkeeper.

"But this period now, where's the next one? One of my best friends is the manager at Southend [Kieron Dyer], who gives me big updates. He's been over the moon with him [Duncan].

"When I've seen him, I've been really happy with him. The National League will test you, it will test your toughness, there's no protection for goalkeepers, so I think it's a brilliant part of his development.

"The more you see him and you see him live then it makes it clear if we think he's going to be ready in the next couple of years. He might not be ready right now but we always have to have one eye on the future."

Wales, who are looking to preserve their place in the Nations League's top tier, face Norway in Oslo on Saturday, 14 November before finishing their campaign at home against Portugal the following Tuesday.

Wales are third in Group A4, with their only win from four matches so far coming against World Cup quarter-finalists Norway in Cardiff last month.

Bellamy's side could still finish in second, third or fourth place.

A top-two spot would take Wales to the Nations League quarter-finals in March 2027.

Finishing third would mean a relegation play-off against a League B team in March while finishing bottom of the group would result in either a relegation play-off or direct relegation, depending on the ranking with other League A groups.

#784. How Carpenter has become Chelsea's surprise star

Ellie Carpenter has played in every WSL game for Chelsea this season

When Chelsea were drawing with Roma at half-time and needed to find a goal from somewhere, Sonia Bompastor opted to bring on a defender instead of a striker.

Some of the head coach's staff questioned her decision - but Bompastor was proven right to trust Ellie Carpenter.

The Australian scored within six minutes as Chelsea went on to win 2-0 and has made a key impact for the Blues on several occasions this season.

"I made the final decision and someone in my technical staff said: 'But we need to score, and you are bringing on a defensive player?'" said Bompastor.

"We laughed after the game because I said: 'Right now, she's scoring a lot of goals, so I don't know if she's a more defensive or attacking player!'

"It worked so it's good. I was confident Ellie would create a lot in the second half."

So why has Carpenter been so effective for Chelsea this season?

Watch Carpenter score as Chelsea thrash Charlton 6-0 in the WSL

Unbeaten Chelsea are top of the Women's Super League table, having only dropped points in their opening weekend draw with Aston Villa.

Carpenter has started all but one of their WSL matches and has netted four goals from a full-back or wing-back position.

In Sunday's 6-0 win at Charlton, Carpenter scored in the 13th minute, won the most tackles (three) and made the most ball recoveries (12) of any Chelsea player.

Only Khadija Shaw, Lauren Hemp and Victoria Pelova have had more touches in the opposition box than Carpenter's 56 this season.

And only Manchester City winger Hemp and Tottenham's Drew Spence have created more chances from open play in the WSL than Carpenter.

"She has been brilliant this season and she has that attacking prowess," former England striker Ellen White said on the Women's Football Weekly podcast.

"She has comfort behind her because she has trust in the other defenders and midfielders to give her the licence to go forward.

"I love her celebrations too! Opposition [teams] target players who are most prolific, but Chelsea have four or five who can score from anywhere on the pitch."

Carpenter arrived from Lyon in 2025 where she had worked with Chelsea boss Bompastor and won the Champions League together in 2022.

She was known to be an attacking full-back, like fellow Blues defender Lucy Bronze, and this season has become accustomed to the right wing-back position.

It has worked for Chelsea with Bronze moving inside as part of a back three and they have conceded just four goals this season, the fewest of any WSL side.

Carpenter's success at the other end of the pitch has been clear, but she has not reneged on her defensive duties - ranking second in the squad for successful tackles made.

Ellie Carpenter ranks first at Chelsea this season for touches in the opposition box and for successful passes in the final third

Carpenter has always been a threat for Chelsea, but in her first season in the WSL a regular criticism was that she could be wasteful with her crosses.

That is something Bompastor thinks the 26-year-old has improved on and means she is contributing to more goals - scoring four and assisting one.

The Australian has also created 19 chances in the WSL this season and has played 141 successful passes in the final third, the most by any Chelsea player.

"Ellie is performing at a really good level. She has goals from her left foot too which is unusual," said Frenchwoman Bompastor.

"She is able to impact the game. The way we want to play as a team, she is really important out of possession and in possession.

"In possession, she always has the mindset and mentality to go forward. She has a lot of pace and is improving a lot in terms of her technical aspects.

"She is now able to deliver really good crosses, to be in the box and be clinical to score goals. I'm not sure she can have a bigger impact than what she is right now."

#783. Bayern Munich's Kenya friendly highlights Africa's growing pull for global sport

Bayern Munich are to open Nairobi's new Raila Odinga International Stadium against Ajax as Kenya prepares for AFCON 2027. The match highlights Africa's growing sports ambitions — and questions over cost and legacy.

Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich are to travel to Nairobi, Kenya during the winter break to play a friendly that opens the newly finished Raila Odinga International Stadium in the capital city. The German side will face Ajax Amsterdam as the game acts as part of the country's preparations for the 2027 African Cup of Nations (AFCON), which will be held in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania next summer.

"Bayern has millions of fantastic fans in Africa with whom we feel a close connection – it's a continent with a huge passion for football," Rouven Kasper, Bayern board member for marketing and sales, said in a club statement.

"We will be making a further contribution to raising the profile of the Bundesliga and are very much looking forward to this special event."

The news is just the latest venture into global sports investing in Africa. Earlier this month, Formula 1 announced it was returning to the continent after Rwanda secured the rights for a deal from the early 2030s onwards. In September, World Athletics revealed Nairobi would host the World Championships in 2029. It will be the first time the event has been held in Africa.

Simon Chadwick, a business management and program director at the African School of Economics, believes that over the last two decades the professionalization and industrialization of sports has begun to emerge in Africa.

"Countries like Rwanda, Kenya, Morocco and obviously, South Africa, if we go back to the last decade of the previous century, have increasingly begun to deploy sport as a policy instrument," Chadwick told DW, adding Senegal and Egypt to the list.

"There are these image and reputational benefits which very often are bundled up as soft power. It's about attractiveness and appeal and engagement," said Chadwick.

"It's almost like a kind of professionalization, industrialization and politicization of sport that we're seeing elsewhere in the world has now arrived in Africa. We are seeing a much greater sense of kind of self-determination within Africa to do this," he added.

"This is not just about sport. It is also about diplomacy and bilateral trade, but also about the broader economic and industrial context within which sport sits."

For Kenya specifically, the building of the stadium is in line with the housing and sports infrastructural development that has been so heavily promoted under President William Ruto. Hosting this game is a symbol of the development currently happening in Nairobi.

"The bigger picture is that Nairobi now is positioning itself as a as an alternative sports venue," Richard Wanjohi, Editorial and Research Lead at the African Sports and Creative Institute (ASCI), told DW.

"I think we have seen what Kigali has done over the last number of years. For us to then come back into this conversation as a major city that can host such an event, it's huge. A few weeks later, we'll have the rugby sevens series again and then ultimately, the Africa Cup of Nations in July."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Chadwick believes that unlike Rwanda, Kenya's relative stability and pre-existing tourist industry allows for a more natural development of sports investment.

"This is not Kenya trying to build a tourism industry through an engagement in sport. I think it's an extension of what Kenya has been doing for a number of years through sport."

Combined with being a multi-sport country - athletics, rugby, football, volleyball – Wanjohi believes Kenya is ready to make the most of that performance on the field or track.

"It's about time that we also host the world and show them that we can do this from a hosting perspective, but also from developing infrastructure that is ready to host such sports events," Wanjohi said.

"It's beyond just saying that we have the talent that is already in the sport, but it's saying that we have the infrastructure, we have the skills, we have the capability to host this as any other African, if not global nation."

However, Ruto's government has been criticized over taxation, unemployment and its handling of dissent. Given that this stadium cost approximately €375 million ($418 million), it is perhaps no surprise that questions are being asked about the decision to invest in major sports infrastructure.

"People are asking, we are a struggling economy. There are a lot of other issues that could be addressed, like the education sector, health and all that. How did we get that money and be able to make that provision? Also interestingly, is that there's an appearance fee that is going to be paid to both Bayern and Ajax," said Wanjohi, who added there was also some frustration that the opening game was not given to local teams or even the national side.

Ultimately, the timing of this also matters. While many sports fans in the country are excited, others are critical.

"The government knows that this is almost like a campaign tool. We have an election coming up in August next year so the government or the president of the day obviously wants to use as much leverage of such an event to milk it for all it's worth," Wanjohi added.

"So the two different schools of thought are: It's a good thing to have, but at what cost are we doing it at and is it in the public interest as well?"

The proof will be in what the legacy of events like Bayern Munich's friendly in Nairobi brings Kenyan football. The feeling in late 2026 though, is largely optimistic.

"I guess the acid test is that many African nations carry with them the baggage from the past that this is just trophy asset investment that is ultimately going to create white, white elephant infrastructure," Chadwick said.

"But having spoken to people in Kenyan sport, in the industry itself, it seems to me that there is a genuine appetite for sports to become a genuine and legitimate driver of economic activity."

Janek Speight contributed reporting for this article.

#782. NFL's Jack Campbell Breaks Silence After Suffering Serious Neck Injury

Following Detroit Lions star Jack Campbell’s serious neck injury during the team’s Nov. 1 game, which appeared to leave him unable to move, the linebacker shared a positive update on his mobility.

Jack Campbell is calling a huddle of his own.

Three days after the Detroit Lions linebacker suffered an immobilizing neck injury and was carried off the field on a stretcher, he broke his silence to deliver a positive update.

“I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time,” Campbell shared in a statement to the Lions’ Instagram Nov. 4. “I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body.”

Still, the 26-year-old added, “I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.”

Since sustaining the injury during the fourth quarter of the team’s 19-15 triumph over the Minnesota Vikings—which left him lying face down on the field, seemingly unable to move at the time—Campbell noted he’s been leaning on his faith in God.

“I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan,” the athlete continued. “I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we’ll get through this.”

Amid his recovery, the University of Iowa alum also emphasized how grateful he and his family—including his wife Megan and their 4-month-old son Cooper—are for the “overwhelming” support they’ve received from fans.

Plus, Campbell gave a special shoutout to the medical staff who have treated him.

“I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field,” he wrote. “I know those were difficult moments, and I'm incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I'll never forget.”

As the NFL star put it, “From the bottom of my heart, thank you.”

While sharing that he plans to “approach this challenge” with the “toughness, resilience and grit” that Detroit is built upon, Campbell turned his focus to his team.

“To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you,” he shared. “This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I'm proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn't ask to be surrounded by a better group of people.”

For all the details to know about Campbell’s neck injury, keep reading…

Jack Campbell was injured during the Detroit Lions’ Nov. 1 game against the Minnesota Vikings

In the fourth quarter of the teams' match-up, Campbell tackled opponent T.J. Hockenson—his third tackle of the game—and was hit on the way down.

He lay face-down on the field, unable to move after the play, and had to be carried off on a backboard by medical personnel.

Campbell was rushed to a nearby hospital to have his neck evaluated

A reporter present at the game called Campbell’s hit the “scariest moment” he’d ever witnessed at Ford Field in a Nov. 1 post on X. He also confirmed that Campbell’s wife Megan Campbell and their baby boy Cooper, who was born in July 2026, were brought down to the field to accompany the player in an ambulance.

Lions coach Dan Campbell—who has no relation to the linebacker—said the team was “thinking about him” in a post-game interview, but had no information to share.

In a post on X following the game, the Detroit Lions confirmed that Campbell was brought “to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury.”

Campbell has remained hospitalized following his injury

On Nov. 2, the Detroit Lions confirmed that Campbell was being closely monitored at the hospital.

“Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital,” the team wrote in a post on X. “Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time.”

Lions coach says Campbell’s recovery update is “positive”

In a press conference one day after Campbell’s injury, Coach Campbell confirmed a heartening update on his player’s recovery.

“It’s positive,” he said. “Your prayers are working. Please continue to do that. We’ll leave it at that. Just continue to pray for him but it is positive news on Jack.”

Coach Campbell calls player an “unbelievable person”

While addressing his player’s injury, the Detroit Lions coach emphasized Campbell’s impact on the team, especially after he was tapped as team captain for this season.

“I don’t even know if I can put it into words,” Dan said during a press conference Nov. 2. “You get voted captain, that says a ton, especially with this group of guys that has been assembled. He earned every bit of that. He’s trustworthy, he’s dependable. He’d give you the shirt off his back. He’s just all heart, man. All effort."

As he put it, “There’s not a man on this team that doesn’t respect Jack Campbell and care about him,”

In an appearance on 97.1 The Ticket Radio Show Nov. 3, Coach Campbell shared an update on his player’s recovery.

“It’s not easy because he’s going to always be on our minds over here,” he said. “The good news is he is improving.”

Campbell breaks silence, says he is "very optimistic" about progress

The linebacker shared a positive update Nov. 4, noting he is "encouraged by the progress" he has made in the three days since his injury.

“I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body,” he wrote in a statement shared to the Detroit Lions' Instagram. "I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.”

#780. Why is it going so wrong for Le Bris at Sunderland?

Regis Le Bris - post-match interview - Coventry City v Sunderland

Dinamo Zagreb under the lights at the Stadium of Light on Bonfire Night.

These should be exciting times for Sunderland and their fans, who before this season had been starved of European football for more than half a century.

Instead there is a concern the club's Europa League campaign, which includes a trip to AC Milan in December, has become a hindrance after the team's poor domestic start to the season.

Last season's surprise Premier League package are rooted to the bottom of the table, with just one win and six defeats from nine games.

Will a game against the champions of Croatia on Thursday (20:00 GMT) serve as a welcome distraction before Sunday's visit of Chelsea?

When Sunderland won at Stamford Bridge last season in their ninth game back after promotion, the Black Cats sat second in the table after an electrifying start.

After nine games this season, it is a very different story.

Questions are being asked about the long-term future of manager Regis le Bris - the man who masterminded Sunderland's return to Europe for the first time in 53 years.

So after last season's impressive seventh-placed finish, why are Sunderland struggling this time round?

Following last Saturday's 3-1 defeat at Coventry City, captain Granit Xhaka questioned the team's "courage", weeks after France defender Nordi Mukiele claimed the side had become "arrogant".

BBC Sport understands Le Bris' job is not in immediate danger and he will be given more time to turn things around.

The Frenchman, in charge since July 2024, is Sunderland's longest-serving manager since Steve Bruce, who was in charge between June 2009 and November 2011.

Le Bris has credit in the bank for winning promotion and then claiming a European spot.

This season he has managed to propel the Black Cats into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, where they face fellow Premier League strugglers Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park.

But how long will Sunderland's hierarchy remain patient if the club, two points from safety, stay anchored in the bottom three?

"They ended last season quite well to get into Europe and that felt really historic," former Sunderland loan signing Nedum Onuoha told BBC Sport.

"But there was talk then that maybe he [Le Bris] wasn't quite the guy.

"Sunderland fans who probably had their doubts last season, I really doubt that they will be thinking he is the manager long term."

French football expert Julien Laurens added about former Lorient boss Le Bris: "This is not looking good.

"I look at Sunderland and I'm not seeing him find the solutions to turn things around. For me that is really worrying."

Sunderland's paradox - San Siro trip amid relegation battle

Sunderland's only Premier League win this season was on 30 August, a 1-0 victory at home to Fulham

Sunderland, who were playing in League One as recently as 2022, were lauded as one of the stories of last season, after doing the double over Chelsea and fierce rivals Newcastle, as well as holding both Arsenal and Manchester City at home.

The numbers suggest repeated success was always going to be difficult.

Only relegated Burnley and Wolves had a lower Expected Goals difference - comparing the amount of good chances created to those chances created against them - than Sunderland last campaign.

How about that dreaded second-season syndrome then. Is it even a thing?

Last season Sunderland and Leeds became the 53rd and 54th promoted sides to survive in the Premier League.

Of the previous 52, only 11 were relegated the following season (21%). The vast majority of promoted teams that stay up do not suffer from second-season syndrome.

With three-quarters of the Premier League season to go, Sunderland will rightly argue there is plenty of time to save themselves.

Yet those heady days of 12 months ago must feel a long way off.

Two of Sunderland's seven league goals this season have come from the penalty spot, while they have finished with 10 men in defeats by Arsenal (Reinildo Mandava sent off), Bournemouth (Kevin Danso sent off) and Coventry (Omar Alderete sent off).

Meanwhile, Sunderland have failed to score a first-half goal in seven of their nine league games.

"Having been promoted many will have believed Sunderland exceeded expectations by finishing in the European places last season," added Onuoha, who made 31 Premier League appearances for the club in 2010-11.

"This season it is five points from nine games with seven goals scored. That speaks for itself in some ways - especially when three of those seven goals came in one game [a 3-5 defeat at Manchester City].

"It doesn't feel at the minute that things are heading in the right direction."

Where is it all going wrong for Sunderland?

Sunderland spent Â£161m on 15 new players after winning promotion to the Premier League in the summer of 2025.

This time round, just Â£60m was invested on five players.

Most fans, however, will have been delighted to keep hold of experienced captain Xhaka and forward Brian Brobbey, who scored seven league goals last season before going on to score three for the Netherlands at the World Cup.

Brobbey, who has signed a new contract until 2031, has yet to score since returning from a hamstring injury, while former Arsenal midfielder Xhaka was downbeat after last weekend's defeat at newly promoted Coventry.

"I don't know exactly what the problem is," said the Switzerland midfielder.

"Is it concentration? Is it other things? We are bottom of the league but in football you need to think positive and to show courage as well.

Carl Jenkinson, who was at Arsenal with Xhaka, told BBC Sport his former team-mate's remarks were "concerning".

"He seemed really deflated and that is very unlike Granit," added the former full-back, who made 41 Premier League appearances for the Gunners between 2011 and 2019.

Laurens said the form of Xhaka and Mukiele, who helped Sunderland towards 11 clean sheets in the top flight last season, had dipped significantly this season.

"They are the leaders and they are way below the levels they had," he added. "The first one to pay the price [for the team's poor form] is usually the manager."

Sunderland are without a win in seven Premier League games

For many, the reason for Sunderland's current struggles appears obvious - the added demand of Europe.

Their first European campaign since 1973 means at least eight games in the Europa League. Unlike in the Premier League, Sunderland have started well in Europe, winning two and drawing one of their first three league phase matches.

"Europe is great," added Laurens. "Sunderland fans will be travelling to Milan, it's wonderful.

"It could be a distraction for the players - especially the ones who have never played in Europe before. It's less time to practise on the training pitch.

"You play Thursday-Sunday and that's a very different dynamic to what Sunderland had last season."

On Wednesday, Le Bris described Sunderland as having "growing pains" this season.

He added: "Is it unexpected? I would say no.

"We are experiencing probably the most demanding challenge Sunderland have ever faced - Premier League, Europa League, quarter-final in the Carabao Cup, FA Cup later.

"It's a new journey - not for everyone because many of our players experienced this situation before, but it's still a new group, one year together.

"I think we are still competitive. We trust our team, our level, but repeating performances is different, this is the new step."

Sunderland have lost two and drawn one of their three Premier League games after playing in Europe.

They could certainly do with beating Chelsea on Sunday after playing Dinamo Zagreb to lift the mood.

Otherwise it is going to be an unhappy international break for Sunderland and their passionate fanbase.

#779. Cardi B Reveals Name of Baby No. 4, Her First With Stefon Diggs

Cardi B announced the name of her and NFL player Stefon Diggs' baby boy, who she revealed last November that they had welcomed.

Cardi B revealed the name of her and NFL player Stefon Diggs' baby boy in honor of his first birthday. While Cardi shares kids Kulture, 8, Wave, 5, and Blossom, 2, with ex Offset, her youngest son is her first child with the New England Patriots wide receiver.

"Happy 1st birthday to Grey Marsean Diggs!!" Cardi wrote on Instagram Nov. 4 alongside sweet pictures of Grey. "It’s only been 1 year since meeting you but it feels like I’ve had you at my side forever. I carried you through one of the most uncertain high pressured times of my life but having you inside of me through it all gave me a extra strength."

That’s why her little guy’s name serves as a special reminder to keep her spirits up.

“I was growing you inside of me and at the same time you were giving me life!” she added. “You gave a new meaning to what a Grey day feels like. You light up my life and every room with your smile your laugh and your precious spirit.”

And, naturally, the mom of four made sure her son’s first Halloween had a sweet link to his moniker. After all, she also shared an adorable pic of the toddler sporting scrubs while sitting in front of a Grey’s Anatomy sign.

The "Hello" rapper’s post also marked the reveal of her baby's birth date. Last year, she shared that she welcomed her newest addition through a message marking her life changes in November.

"A new baby into my world, and one more reason to be the best version of me, one more reason to love me more than anything else or anyone else so I can continue giving my babies the love and life they deserve," she captioned her post at the time, a video of her strutting and striking poses to her song "Hello." She continued, "This next chapter is Me vs. Me!"

And the next chapter already looks good on her. Just hours after the announcement that she's now a mom of four, Cardi stepped out with Stefon for the launch party of baby brand Cybex’s flagship store in New York City, rocking a dramatic all-black ensemble featuring a corseted puffer coat, bubble skirt and fur detailing.

While Cardi opted to keep her lips sealed regarding her baby boy's name at the time, she did hint that it was one she really loved.

"I'm not sharing the name yet," she told Highsnobiety at the Cybex event. "It's cute."

While the name stayed under wraps, the 34-year-old did share a bit into what her birth and post-partum experience has been like, adding, "You know, I was a little bit on bed rest because that baby, oh, that baby was heavy."

However, her toughness is what she hopes her children will learn from her.

"I will stand up for myself," she said of how she leads by example. "Sometimes people be like, 'Oh no avoid it.' No, I will stand up for myself. Then my kids can see that they mama ain't no punk."

For more Cardi B moments that will make your say "Okurrr," read on.

"She broke my vagina," Cardi B told Jimmy Kimmel while recalling the birth of her daughter, Kulture Kiari. "Nobody told me they were gonna stitch my vagina."

"Shoes? $1,200. These glasses? $400. But bitch, my outfit? $20 dollars bitch," she exclaimed in a since-deleted Instagram post. "Get yourself together bitch. Learn how to budget hoe."

"NOTHING LAST FOREVER EXCEPT BILLS," she declared on Twitter when a fan asked for help choosing a senior quote. To be fair, she's not wrong.

"My boyfriend at the time—he dumped me two weeks before my prom, but I honestly think it was because he didn't want to pay for the limo, but then that night…forget it," she told Jimmy Fallon and John Mulaney on The Tonight Show. "The limo that I ended up with—I didn't rented it…I just got in a limo and just…forget it. I can't get into it. Kids watch me now."

"Once you start making money, everybody wants you to be their kid's godmother," she quipped on The Tonight Show.

"I want to thank my fans—Bardi Gang—because even when I'm wrong they be like, 'She still right' and I want to thank my haters, too, because they be downloading my stuff so they can hear it and talk crap about it, but it benefits me!" she said while accepting the Best New Artist Award at the 2018 iHeartRadio Music Awards.

"I'm just a regular, degular, shmegular girl from the Bronx," the former reality star has said often on Love & Hip Hop.

"If he has sex with you more than five times, he loves you," she told BET in 2017.

"I'm feeling good, I'm feeling nervous, overwhelmed—everything!" she told E!'s Giuliana Rancic at the 2018 Grammys. "Butterflies in my stomach and vagina!"

"I get really happy when people see me perform and they're rapping my music, but it's a different feeling when you're dancing and the men throwing you money because you look good," she told New York in 2017. "It's just like when the rice is getting thrown at the bride."

"Sometimes I get a little discouraged, and I wonder how it is going to be next year, but it seems like everybody already predicting where I'm gonna be next year, and it's just like f--king farther than my a--hole," she told New York in 2017.

In a candid Instagram video, Cardi said, "You know, as I get older and I wax more I notice that my mustache is getting thicker. But it's cool though, cause b--ches with good mustaches got good p---y."

#775. Andrew Garfield Addresses Family Plans Amid Monica Barbaro Romance

Andrew Garfield, who has been dating Monica Barbaro since 2024, addressed whether he still has plans to start a family and have any kids of his own, saying, “It’s mysterious to me.”

Andrew Garfield isn’t sure if he wants to keep spinning his family’s web.

The Amazing Spider-Man alum recently detailed whether he still has plans to start a family or have kids in the near future, admitting he still isn’t feeling definitive either way.

“I’m the same as everyone else who’s even remotely cognizant of where we are and where we’re heading,” Garfield explained in an interview with GQ published Nov. 4. “I look at my friends who do have kids and the beauty of it obviously, but also the struggle of it and the inescapable agony of young people’s longing to belong to the screen rather than belong to the real world.”

Garfield—who has been in a relationship with Monica Barbaro since 2024—admitted that he has no Spidey sense when it comes to whether having kids is a good idea.

“It gives me pause for sure, like any person, I suppose,” he continued. “That being said, there is that kind of biological imperative, and there is that just kind of instinct, and there’s an image that your life with for so long—I have, anyway—of the concept of being a dad and going on an adventure.”

At 43, Garfield has been more vocal with the concept of having kids at some point.

“I’m childless,” he said during a September appearance on the Smartless podcast. “I’m not entirely proud of that. I would love to have kids. I would love to start a family.”

But while the We Live in Time actor—who previously dated Emma Stone and Dr. Kate Tomas—has taken off his mask when it comes to discussing the potential of having future children, he recently drew the line when it came to discussing his romantic life.

“It feels like a violation of my inner world, my private world,” Garfield explained in an interview with Vanity Fair last year. “I thought maybe that would soften at some point, but I’m very surprised to say that it hasn’t.”

He firmly acknowledged, “I have never, and I won’t ever, speak about or confirm or deny anything about my personal life with anyone.”

If you're Spidey senses are tingling for more details, keep reading for a look back at Garfield's love life.

If you've been on the internet, then you're aware those romance rumors about Andrew Garfield and Monica Barbaro aren't a complete unknown.The We Live in Time actor and the A Complete Unknown actress sparked dating speculation after a social media user shared a video of the pair attending Jonathan Bailey's performance of Richard II at London's Bridge Theatre Feb. 19.However, this wouldn't be the first time Monica and Andrew had crossed paths. They were also photographed alongside Eddie Redmayne and W Magazine's Editor-at-Large Lynn Hirschberg at the outlet's Annual Best Performances Party in Los Angeles January 4.E! News reached out to Monica and Andrew's reps for comment but didn't hear back.

Fans' social networks alerted them to Andrew's romance with Dr. Kate Tomas after the two were seen on an apparent double date with Phoebe Bridgers and Bo Burnham in March 2024.“I am in a new relationship," the spiritual mentor said on a June 2024 episode of her podcast The Friday Emails without naming names, per The Sunday Times, "and I’m in love and I’m really happy."However, she didn't love that the media mostly focused on her relationship with the Oscar nominee."It’s frustrating that no matter how accomplished or impactful a woman is, it’s always going to be more interesting if they are in a relationship with a man," Kate told The Sunday Times in a July 2024 interview. "I don’t want to sit under anybody’s shadow."Nor did the philosopher want to deal with the barrage of public scrutiny and judgment that came with dating in the spotlight.The way she saw it, photographers "will take maybe 150 pictures, then they choose the four where you look worst,” she continued, calling out the “misogynistic nature of that interest—criticism of how a woman looks, of what [she] does for work."However, Kate and Andrew's relationship didn't last long. In October 2024, she confirmed on Instagram that they "broke up months ago."

While neither Olivia Brower nor Andrew ever publicly commented on dating rumors, The Amazing Spider-Man star and the model found themselves tangled in a web of speculation after Page Six published photos of them hugging and appearing to share a kiss in January 2024.

Nearly three months after Alyssa Miller and Andrew first sparked romance rumors in November 2021 by walking hand in hand in New York, E! News confirmed the 1984 alum and the model were dating.The two "were certainly happy in each other's company," a source told E! News in February 2022 after Andrew and Alyssa were spotted on a tennis court in Malibu, Calif., "and not hiding anything."At the SAG Awards later that month, the pair made their red carpet debut as a couple.But in April 2022, a source close to the situation confirmed to E! News that Andrew and Alyssa had parted ways. Shortly after the news spread, she addressed the topic herself."If you must gossip at least use a cute photo," Alyssa captioned a selfie of the duo. "Lol love you AG."

Aisling Bea and Andrew had fans buzzing after he was photographed with his arm around her at a performance of Hamilton in London in March 2019. Still, the tick, tick... BOOM! actor and comedian never publicly commented on the romance rumors.

In November 2018, fans started to wonder if Rita Ora and Andrew had struck up a romance—with their sightings together, including a Christmas Eve stroll in London, only fueling speculation. Still, the singer and The Social Network star stayed tight lipped on where they stood—with her even dodging a question about whether she preferred Andrew or Tobey Maguire as Spider-Man."You’re making me wake up this morning," she said on a 2019 episode of The Morning Mash Up. "I don’t watch Spider-Man. That’s my answer."But by March 2019—before his sighting with Aisling—reports spread that Andrew and Rita (who is now married to Taika Waititi) split.

Things appeared to be heating up between Susie Abromeit and Andrew as they were spotted kissing on a beach in Malibu, Calif. in September 2018. And earlier that month, the Hacksaw Ridge star and the Jessica Jones actress had been seen at Disneyland together.However, the romance rumors soon fizzled, and neither Andrew nor Susie ever commented on the dating speculation.

Emma Stone and Andrew's bond went from friendly, neighborhood costars to a loving couple after they worked together on The Amazing Spider-Man in 2011."It's a dream to work with him," the Oscar winner said in a 2014 interview with ABC News. "He's obviously one of the greatest actors I think we have alive today, and he's also just a remarkable human being. So, I love him very much."Emma and Andrew gave fans glimpses into their love on red carpets, at award shows, during her 2014 SNL hosting gig and on their many NYC dates (including one where they held up cards championing causes they cared about after spotting photographers).But in 2015, news broke that Emma and Andrew split. Still, the La La Land star—who is now married to Dave McCary— and the Mainstream actor continue to be on good terms.

"We care about each other so much, and that’s a given, that’s kind of this unconditional thing,” he said on a 2017 episode of Vanity Fair's Little Gold Men podcast. “There’s so much love between us and so much respect...I’m her biggest fan as an artist. So for me, it’s been bliss to be able to watch her success and watch her bloom into the actress that she is. And it’s also been wonderful to have that kind of support for each other. It’s nothing but a beautiful thing.”

"I think my girlfriend is proud of me and the fact that I've remained grounded," he told Parade in 2010, the year of the film's debut. "I think I'm just busier. That's the main thing. I haven't got as much time to mope about and complain that I'm bored. She travels with me when she's not working. Whenever we have time, we're together. When I'm on my own, you'd find me in the ocean surfing."

But after three years together, the Under the Banner of Heaven alum and the Raising Hope actress parted ways.

#773. West Ham took too long to sack Nuno and now must trust Parker to do what he does best | Jacob Steinberg

Forget speculation over how a Parker-led side would fare in the Premier League and let the man who has taken three clubs up do his work again

It has taken West Ham six months to come to their senses and sack Nuno Espírito Santo, but at least the decision has arrived early enough to revive their hopes of automatic promotion.

Dithering was no longer an option after the dismal performance against West Brom last Saturday.

West Ham, eighth in the Championship and four points off the top two, had to act after a second consecutive home defeat. They are in danger of slipping into a battle for a playoff spot and needed to move on from Nuno after just over a year of his confused, passive football.

Nuno did a terrible job after replacing Graham Potter as manager in September 2025. The 52-year-old had 33 games to save West Ham from relegation and failed. He has the most expensive squad in the Championship but his side have not lived up to their billing as title favourites and their stuttering form has exposed the folly of not sacking Nuno at the end of last season.

David Sullivan, then the club’s largest shareholder, wanted a change. But Daniel Kretinsky favoured continuity and looked to capitalise on the shifting power dynamics in the boardroom. Karren Brady had stepped down as vice-chair in April – Karim Virani replaced her in an interim role – and there was further upheaval when Sullivan resigned as joint-chair and a director of the club to fight what he described as “false allegations” regarding his personal conduct.

Sullivan bears most culpability for West Ham’s relegation. He still owns a 40% stake but is no longer on the board and West Ham are better off without him dictating key decisions. Equally, though, where Sullivan was not mistaken was in wanting Nuno gone. Kretinsky got his first big call wrong. At least the Czech billionaire has given Nuno’s replacement time to get the team back on track. The task falls to Scott Parker, who has been on the market since leaving Burnley last April. Parker is regarded as a “safe” appointment and has been on West Ham’s radar for a while.

Some wanted the former England midfielder in the summer and his name was mentioned again when West Ham failed to win their first three league games. Patience was wearing thin. A subsequent run of four wins in a row swiftly proved a false dawn.

West Ham have not had the right mindset. They have two wins from their past six games and have often started playing only after going a goal down. A 6-0 win against Wrexham was a highlight but victory at Lincoln by the same scoreline came with the caveat that the Imps received two red cards before half-time.

There was no identity under Nuno. West Ham are unbeaten on the road and won 1-0 at the then table-topping Swansea last month but it has been hard to tell Nuno broke the Football League transfer record with the £22m signing of the Belgium midfielder Arne Engels from Celtic. Even Jarrod Bowen, who was convinced to sign a new deal in the summer, has been off colour. Nuno’s tactics mean the winger, West Ham’s top scorer, is often crowded out.

West Ham were lopsided against West Brom. Enough was enough. Kretinsky, who is not at every game, was unimpressed when he attended West Ham’s 3-2 defeat by Southampton a week earlier. He pays attention to the views of Bowen, Tomas Soucek and Mark Noble, the technical director and former club captain.

Nuno, whose substitutions were almost as weird as his starting lineups, had lost the players. The mood darkened after the West Brom game. West Ham were easy to play through because of Nuno’s reluctance to use a holding midfielder, an issue exacerbated by his refusal to use Edson Álvarez or Soungoutou Magassa after both sought moves during the summer.

Magassa’s exile has caused disquiet. Not only is a young asset being devalued, a fragile defence is going without enough protection. West Ham have a lot of No 8s but they need a No 6. It is an area for Parker to address. He will also need to work out whether to stick with Mads Hermansen in goal, and the jury is out on summer signings.

One source questions whether West Ham targeted players equipped to handle the intensity of the Championship. Divine Mukasa, the 19-year-old midfielder, is talented but inconsistent. Manor Solomon and Edvin Austbø have flattered to deceive on the left wing. Joël Veltman, the 34-year-old Dutch right-back, has had fitness issues. Adama Boiro, a 24-year-old left‑back on loan from Athletic Bilbao, has not been seen since a cameo against Derby in early September. The three strikers signed by Nuno across two windows have toiled; Pablo Felipe, Taty Castellanos and Joël Piroe have five league goals between them this season.

Nils Koppen, the head of recruitment appointed in the summer, will have to be busy in January, but Parker will hope to have made his impact before the window opens. He is not known for expansive football but he is proven at this level. Parker won promotion with Bournemouth, Burnley and Fulham. The 46-year-old’s track record is clear and it helps that he has an association with West Ham.

Parker, whose all-action playing style made him a fan favourite, knows how difficult it can be in east London. He played in some pretty bad West Ham sides, experienced relegation in 2011 and arrives with the club in a tricky spot again.

It is not the moment to start worrying about Parker’s questionable record as a Premier League manager. What do West Ham do if they go up? Do they stick with Parker? Do they make an instant change? Well, how about they get promoted first? The rest can wait.

#772. Germany news: Merz hopes for Korean reunification at DMZ

Chancellor Friedrich Merz has expressed hope for Korean reunification during a visit to the heavily fortified border. Meanwhile, President Steinmeier has held talks with China's Xi Jinping in Beijing.

Below, you can review the leading headlines from and about Germany from Friday, October 30:

Chancellor Friedrich Merz visits the demilitarized zone between North and South Korea

Merz draws on Germany's own reunification experience, saying division causes suffering

Two German leaders, two parallel missions across Asia.

While President Frank-Walter Steinmeier sought to reinforce ties with China in Beijing, Chancellor Friedrich Merz toured Japan, South Korea and Singapore, promoting closer cooperation among what he calls the world's "middle powers."

Together, the visits highlight Berlin's effort to lower risks without decoupling from China.

Germany's annual inflation rate eased to 2.8% in October from 3.3% in September, with economists pointing to the government's fuel tax cut as the main reason.

Preliminary figures from the Federal Statistical Office showed energy prices rose 12.2% compared with a year earlier, down from 14.9% in September. Services inflation slowed to 2.5%, while food inflation remained at 0.4%.

"The decisive factor was the fuel tax cut," said Silke Tober of the Macroeconomic Policy Institute. The reduction took effect in October and runs through December, although rising crude oil prices partly offset the savings at the pump.

ING bank economist Carsten Brzeski said higher energy costs had yet to feed through into broader price increases. Unlike during the 2022 energy crisis, consumers were unwilling or unable to absorb substantially higher prices, he said.

But economists warned the relief could prove temporary. "Gas and oil prices have risen significantly again in recent weeks," said Stephanie Schoenwald, an economist at Germany's state-owned development bank KfW, citing continuing conflicts and lower inventories.

German President's Frank-Walter Steinmeier latest trip to Asia was intended to provide more clarity. Amid a delicate period, Steinmeier sought a balancing act in China between respect and criticism.

It was a state visit of a kind rarely seen today. For four days, Steinmeier traveled across the country: from Hefei, where the German automaker Volkswagen's China operations are headquartered, through historic villages and the imposing landscapes of the Yellow Mountains. He also visited several points of interest of Chinese history, art, and science, and finally, he headed to Tiananmen Square in the heart of Beijing's political center.

Steinmeier—who is set to leave office in March 2027— spoke as a statesman and diplomat on matters of German and European interest. Chinese President Xi Jinping and Steinmeier have known each other for many years, so in this respect, the president was the right man to address even the most difficult issues as a European.

This political balancing act between respect and criticism did not trigger any visible outrage in Beijing.

When he spoke with Chinese leaders about their subsidies for exports to Europe and the related issue of the trade deficit, Xi replied: "I am ready to work together to open a new chapter in the comprehensive strategic partnership between our two countries and to advance the development of global governance."

Just how much willingness lies behind the push for a strategic partnership will become clear during further negotiations between the EU and China.

Xi Jinping seems to understand that a persistent trade deficit with Europe could also become a problem for his country, as an economic crisis in Europe could further strain China's economy.

As "the world's second- and third-largest economies," China and Germany also bear "an important responsibility for the development of relations between China and Europe, as well as for stable growth in the global economy," Xi Jinping said. While that may not sound like a breakthrough yet, it certainly sounds like an understanding.

In contrast to his economic arguments, Steinmeier's political appeals for Beijing to assume more responsibility for the international order fell on deaf ears.

The German president addressed global conflicts and wars on several occasions in Beijing, including Russia's war of aggression in Ukraine. But he received no responses in official statements.

That same evening, the news channel of the Chinese TV network CCTV aired a report that merely covered Steinmeier's visit to a well-known astrophysics institute.

There was no mention of the call for China, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, to do more to promote world peace.

Mitat Özdemir is one of more than 870,000 Turkish workers who were recruited to Germany by a government program between 1961 and 1973. He dealt with tough factory work, language barriers and cultural differences.

Six decades later, he and his family still live in Germany. How did the program from back then shape their lives and modern Germany?

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Friday visited the Panmunjom truce village at the demilitarized zone (DMZ) separating North and South Korea, briefly standing on the North Korean side inside the barracks.

North and South Korea have been divided since the end of hostilities in the Korean War in 1953, with a border running across the peninsula.

In remarks to reporters, Merz recalled Germany's reunification 36 years ago.

"Let us hope that Korea too gets the chance one day to regain state unity," he said.

"You can also notice it here at this place, how much a country suffers from division and how strong the desire is for reunification, at least in this part of the Korean Peninsula," he said, adding that he had been asked about Germany's reunification experience while visiting Seoul.

North Korea, however, has backed away in recent years from diplomacy with the South, having officially removed language calling for reunification from its constitution while changing the South's status to that of a "hostile state."

A glass cabinet containing memorabilia linked to the 1958 Munich Air Disaster, in which eight Manchester United footballers lost their lives, was smashed and plundered in the Munich suburb of Trudering this week.

The display case on Manchesterplatz forms part of a memorial commemorating the tragedy which occurred when the United team made a refueling stop in Munich while on the way back from a European Cup game in Belgrade, Serbia, on February 6, 1958.

The plane struggled to take off again in the wintery conditions at the old Munich-Riem airport to the east of the city center and, on the third attempt, ploughed off the end of the runway and into a house. Of the 44 people on board, 23 were killed, including eight United players, several journalists and two crew members.

The crash site has become a place of pilgrimage for United supporters and, in 2020, the cabinet was installed on the initiative of the Red Docs Munich – a local Bayern Munich fan club – to house the various memorabilia and tributes left by visitors.

Munich police said the cabinet was broken into on Monday morning between 8 a.m. and 1 p.m. local time (07:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. UTC), with the unknown perpetrators making off with a glass sculpture and several medals.

"They don't understand the damage that they've caused," Ifty Ahmed, chairman of the Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation (MMMF), told the BBC, adding: "Whatever they've taken from inside the showcase, they haven't taken our memories."

The Red Docs Munich arranged for replacement glass to be installed on the same day. The MMMF said Manchester United had offered to pay for the repairs but said the foundation had covered the costs itself.

The joint commemoration of the 1958 disaster and the maintenance of the memorial site has produced extensive and friendly relations between Bayern Munich and Manchester United, who will meet in the Champions League in January.

German politicians have been slow to respond as they wait to see who is likely to comprise the next coalition. Many are also hoping for a government without religious hardliners.

Profits of German luxury car brand Audi for the third quarter came plunged 87% year-on-year to €95 million ($106 million), the Volkswagen subsidiary reported on Friday. This is a drop from €718 million seen in the same quarter last year.

A ban on new Stolpersteine ("stumbling stones") to commemorate victims of the Holocaust in the eastern German town of Heidenau will be upheld after five petitions against the measure were thrown out.

Local councilors from Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) voted together in September to pass the controversial ban on new stones being laid in the town in Saxony, near Dresden.

Petitions against the measure were submitted from across Germany — as well as one from the Netherlands — calling for victims of the Nazi regime to continue to be remembered in Heidenau by way of the small metal plaques embedded in pavements.

"Not everybody has to like the stumbling stones but everyone should have the possibility to lay one in public," one councilor, Michael Schürer, told Germany's Catholic News Agency (KNA), criticizing the rejection of the petitions.

The initiators of the Heidenau ban had argued that, while remembering Holocaust victims remains essential, the placement of Stolpersteine leads to "passersby walking over or even stepping onto the names of the victims." They suggested honoring victims at a local cemetery instead.

The decision of the local Heidenau CDU to join forces with the AfD to pass the motion sparked a nationwide scandal and furthered the debate over the conservatives' commitment to the political "firewall" against the far right.

"We both bear responsibility for the ⁠international order ​and for the conditions under which states in this world maintain and shape their relations," Steinmeier said.

President Xi praised what he called an "all-dimensional strategic partnership" between China and Germany, calling for new cooperation based on stability and mutual benefit.

"This new paradigm sends a positive signal to the world: we favor openness over closure, and cooperation over confrontation," Xi said during opening remarks, emphasizing the start of a "new chapter" in Germany-China ties.

Xi added that he hopes Germany and the European Union will stick by a "rational, pragmatic and friendly" China policy, adding that cooperation outweighs competition and consensus outweighs differences in China-EU relations.

The EU has a massive trade deficit with China, which reached €360 billion ($400.4 billion) last year and is set to exceed that level this year.

Brussels has accused China of unfair economic practices, saying its state subsidies for its industries are creating an unlevel playing field. Germany with its export based economy, the EU's largest, is hit hard by China's manufacturing surplus flooding global markets.

Industry groups say the surge in imports from China is leading to an increasing number of factory closures in the bloc.

Nonetheless, "differences and problems can always be resolved," the Chinese president said.

While German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in South Korea on Friday called for a better rule-based trade order, President Frank-Walter Steinmeier was in the Chinese capital in a bid to smooth out trade disagreements.

In Beijing, Steinmeier called for preserving the "win-win principle" characterizing Sino-German relations, borrowing from the expression "win-win cooperation," one of the most frequently used phrases in Chinese foreign policy statements.

Germany's economic ties with China have gone through a shock in recent years, with Chinese manufacturing growing into sectors once dominated by German firms, and Chinese electric cars taking over market share.

At the start of a meeting with Chinese Premier Li Qiang, Steinmeier cited a recent deal limiting exports of Chinese hybrid cars to the EU in exchange for select tariff cuts on EU exports to China as an example of a "a way to find solutions."

Steinmeier also brought up Germany's growing trade deficit with China, which grew to nearly €90 billion ($100 billion) last year.

Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.

Steinmeier said Germany would work to solve trade problems with China. "We are coming with the intention of maintaining and strengthening the framework for good economic exchange between our two countries," Steinmeier said.

Later in the day, the German president, who occupies a largely ceremonial role without policymaking power, was also recieved by an honor guard alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping.

During his final day of a whirlwind Asia tour this week, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told the Asia-Pacific Conference of German Business in Seoul on Friday that Germany and Europe are ready to cooperate with Asian economies to foster a rules-based economic order.

Merz said the European Union is ready to take the lead in shaping a better deal for countries in Asia feeling the pressure of a destabilized rules-based trade order.

"Competition between the US and China is ramping up. Tariffs, technological decoupling strategies and a tough race for critical raw materials and new technologies are fundamentally changing the rules of our global economy," Merz said.

"These conflicts and systemic shifts in power patterns concern us all. They particularly concern economically aspiring partners in the Indo-Pacific, as well as in Germany and in Europe."

During stops in Singapore and Japan this week, Merz pushed for free trade partnerships and greater European cooperation with Asian economies.

In Singapore on Wednesday, Merz called for a free trade agreement between the EU and the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), a sweeping multilateral free trade agreement connecting the Asia Pacific and the Americas.

The UK is the single European signatory, albeit outside of the EU bloc. The US pulled out during the first administration President Donald Trump in 2017, scuttling the original version, the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP).

"We want to offer opportunities beyond bilateral agreements,"he said in Seoul on Friday.

"We are resolutely joining forces against unilateralism, autocratic power politics and violations of international law," Merz added.

"When supply chains become political pawns, when access to key technologies is obstructed or when efforts to secure raw materials resemble displays of power rather than fair partnerships, this jeopardizes growth, prosperity and ultimately the security of entire regions."

Merz also tried to allay concerns about EU protectionism under the "Made in Europe" scheme intended to protect carmakers.

"There is a fear that we might be facing ‌a new wave of European protectionism - that we are closing ‌ourselves off from other nations," ‌Merz said.

"I take these concerns very seriously. I will carry them back not just to Berlin, ‌but also to Brussels, and I will certainly raise the fact that these concerns were expressed to me quite forcefully here," he added.

Citing Germany as an example, South Korean Prime Minister Han Seong Sook told the conference  "German companies are using Korea as a central hub to expand their presence in the Asia-Pacific region."

The question of who should become Germany's new president is becoming pressing.

Many want to see Germany's first female head of state. Chancellor Friedrich Merz is keeping his cards close to his chest.
