#756. Taylor Swift Shook Off One Concern Before Saying Yes to Toy Story 5

Before Taylor Swift agreed to write the end credits song “I Knew It, I Knew You” for Toy Story 5, she said she confirmed no one else would be kicked off the project in order for her to do it.

However, the Grammy winner recently shared that before she agreed to saddle up and write the original song “I Knew It, I Knew You” for Toy Story 5, she had to make sure no one else would get booted from the project.

That’s because Swift was initially approached about writing the end credits song while she was on her record-breaking Eras Tour, but she put off taking the meeting until months after it ended so that she could rest.

“I was repeatedly asking, ‘I know that it took me a couple months to come back to this project. Be honest: did you guys replace me?’” the 36-year-old recalled of the meeting during a Nov. 1 Q&A. “‘I don't want to kick somebody off of this project that you reached out to after [me] because I understand, but I'm not in the business of doing that.’”

But the “Cardigan” singer soon realized she was patient zero.

“I found out that there was no other person on your mood board,” she said alongside director Andrew Stanton during the joint Q&A. “Everybody said, ‘No, we just decided there wasn't going to be an end credit song [if you didn’t do it].’”

So, Swift went to infinity and beyond to make sure she and her cowriter Jack Antonoff captured the Pixar film’s story.

“When I saw this brilliant film that Andrew made, I realized exactly why he knew I would love it,” she explained. “It's centered around Jesse, who's my favorite character, and it deals with female friendship.”

And as Swift put it, “It's crazy how I could see a way into all the characters in a way, and it was like a struck-by-lightning moment of like, ‘I have to go home, get to my piano, and write this song, because I know exactly what I would want to say if I had you know the privilege of writing for this.’”

To learn about the inspiration behind some of Swift’s other iconic tracks, keep reading…

Before The Life of a Showgirl, the only track Taylor had certainly written about her guy on the Chiefs—save for The Eras Tour “Karma” rewrite, of course—is “So High School,” which the now-engaged couple aptly set their proposal Instagram post to in August 2025.

Although some fans speculate “The Alchemy,” also off The Tortured Poets Department, is about Travis for the football and high school metaphors sprinkled in the track, “So High School” includes a more obvious nod with the lyrics: “Are you going to marry, kiss or kill me? / It’s just a game but really / I’m betting on all three, for us two.”

Indeed, Travis revealed to AfterBuzzTV back in 2016 that “Taylor Swift, would be the kiss,” in a game of “Marry, Kiss, Kill” between her, Ariana Grande and Katy Perry.

As for how Travis feels about the track? Although it’s a tough competition as a Swiftie, it’s his all-time favorite.

“I’m not gonna lie,” he joked of the choice to Access Hollywood in 2024. “I might be a little biased.”

But now that Taylor has found the guy who can call her honey, he's the one she most wants to pay tribute to in verse.

On The Life of a Showgirl, she sang about her now-husband topping her "Wi$h Li$t," serving as her "forever night stand" in "Honey," and turning her sky "Opalite."

And, forgive her, it sounds cocky, but in "Wood," her raciest song yet, she shared how Travis' love was the key that opened her thighs.

Fortunately, Taylor's mom Andrea Swift, "thinks that the song is about superstitions, which it absolutely is," Taylor joked on SiriusXM’s Morning Mash Up after the album's October 2025 release. "That’s the joy of the double entendre. You can read that song for people, and it just goes right over their heads."

But it wasn't hard to grasp who she was calling "the love of my life" on the Encore track "Cleveland!," the title itself an overt nod to Travis' hometown.

Although short-lived, Taylor appeared to write several songs on The Tortured Poets Department about her dalliance with The 1975 frontman in 2023, including the album’s title track which also name drops their mutual pal and collaborator Jack Antonoff.

Other tracks rumored to be about Matty include “Fortnight,” “Down Bad,” and “But Daddy I Love Him,” the latter of which also appears to call out the backlash Taylor received for her relationship with him.

And while Matty told paparazzi, per Entertainment Tonight in 2024 that he hadn’t listened to the album, though he was "sure it’s good," his mother Denise Welch slammed his alleged connection to the breakup ballads.

"You're not allowed to say anything," the Loose Woman cohost said during a 2025 appearance on Watch What Happens Live, "and then she writes a whole album about it."

For more on Matty’s place in Taylor’s catalogue, read here.

It's actually sweet all the time an unnamed rival has spent on the singer. Or, at least, that's what Taylor conveyed in The Life of a Showgirl track "Actually Romantic."

Rather than share her praise for Travis or even an ex-lover, the musician actually sings about a person who "high-fived my ex and then you said you're glad he ghosted me. Wrote me a song saying it makes you sick to see my face / Some people might be offended / But it's actually sweet."

Fans were quick to say the clues pointed toward Charli XCX, who opened for Taylor on her Reputation Tour and is close with Taylor's ex Matty and his now-wife Gabbriette Bechtel.

Another tell was Charli's 2024 brat track "Sympathy Is a Knife," in which the British musician—married to Matty's The 1975 bandmate George Daniel—sings, "Don’t wanna see her backstage at my boyfriend’s show. Fingers crossed behind my back / I hope they break up real quick."

Good thing for Brittany Mahomes, Taylor likes her friends canceled. Because fans feel the singer was thinking of the former soccer player—wed to Travis' teammate Patrick Mahomes—or onetime BFF Blake Lively when she wrote about standing by a pal's side when the whole world has seemingly turned on them.

But really the person at the crux of The Life of a Showgirl track is Taylor herself, who felt her reputation took several hits after her very public 2016 feud with Kanye West and then-wife Kim Kardashian.

"Having had my own experiences with mass judgment and being at the center of many dramatic, scandalous moments in my career, where people were all weighing in at once or at least it felt like that," she told Amazon Music, "having had those experiences, it makes me move through the world a little bit differently."

And now she wants to gift that what-doesn't-kill-you-makes-you-stronger mentality to others. As the lyrics suggest, Taylor continued, "I don't just naturally cast people aside just because other people decide they don't like them. I make my own decisions about people based on how they treat me within my life and their actions."

Amid their six-year relationship, Taylor penned several songs about—and with—the Conversations With Friends star. Shortly after the pair's relationship was confirmed in 2016, she released Reputation, which included several songs presumably about Joe such as “Call It What You Want,” “Dress,” and “King of My Heart.”

On Lover, Taylor also included the track "Cornelia Street," a nod to the New York City rental she was living in during the early months of their romance. Elsewhere in her discography, fans believe Taylor also penned "invisible string," on folklore about her romance with Joe, as well as Midnights' "Sweet Nothing" and its bonus track 'You’re Losing Me," which her producer Jack confirmed was written two years before Taylor's 2023 breakup with Joe.

Joe is one of the many people in Taylor’s life who has also become her cowriter on songs, earning credits on folklore and evermore songs like "betty," "champagne problems," "exile" and others under the pseudonym William Bowery.

"It was really the most accidental thing to happen in lockdown," the Brutalist alum told GQ of the cowriting credits in 2022. "It was just messing around on a piano and singing badly and being overheard and then thinking, you know, what if we tried to get to the end of it together?"

For more songs inspired by Joe, see here.

Following the infamous—and later revealed to be edited—phone call leak in 2016 between Kanye and Taylor over a reference he made to her on his The Life of Pablo album, Taylor has subtly clapped back at the divorced couple more than once.

As recently as 2024, Taylor penned "thanK you aIMee" likely about Kim, given she capitalized letters in the track's title to spell out her name. (In another variant of the TTPD album, she changed the letters to capitalize "YE" in the track, as an apparent nod toward the rapper.)

Prior to TTPD, Taylor also sprinkled hits against Kim and Kanye for the "Famous" feud, with "Mad Woman," on folklore, where she sings, "Women like hunting witches too / Doing your dirtiest work for you / It’s obvious that wanting me dead has really brought you two together."

Taylor’s first Reputation single "Look What You Made Me Do," was also a nod to the public fallout, as well as "This Is Why We Can’t Have Nice Things," in which she sings about a once-repaired friendship fracturing again.

But, of course, Taylor's musical inspirations from Kanye date back to that 2009 MTV VMA incident, when he interrupted her speech for Best Female Video at the Video Music Awards. In Speak Now’s "Innocent," she forgives Kanye for the viral moment, which earned him backlash from figures as prominent as then-president Barack Obama.

"It's OK / Life is a tough crowd," Taylor sings on the track, going on to reference his age at the time of the VMAs. "32 and still growing up now / Who you are is not what you did / You’re still an innocent."

For a thorough dive into Taylor’s beef with Kanye, see here.

Taylor and the Loki actor may have only had a short-lived romance in the summer of 2016, but it did inspire more than one track for the "Karma" singer. Indeed, many fans speculated that "Getaway Car," and "High Infidelity" are about the timeline of their romance in comparison to her relationship with Calvin Harris. She and the DJ split in June 2016 after one year of dating, the same month she sparked rumors with Tom.

In both songs, Taylor sings about how a relationship born out of slight infidelity is doomed from the start.

While fans are sure these three are the ones who made up the "Getaway Car" sideshow, neither Taylor, nor Calvin or Tom have addressed the inspiration for the songs.

Although Taylor shut down any speculation that she wrote songs about her romance with the One Direction alum, there are a lot of subtle references to the "Watermelon Sugar" singer on 1989.

"Style," is the most obvious nod to Harry, simply for the title, as well as "Out of the Woods," and bonus track "Wonderland," which references a "Cheshire cat smile"—which many fans see as a nod to Harry’s hometown of Holmes Chapel in Cheshire, England.

Meanwhile, the 1989 vault track "Is It Over Now?" paints a vivid picture of the moment Taylor knew her romance with Harry was done for good.

"Blue dress on a boat," she sings in reference to the infamous January 2013 photo of her after the couple’s alleged breakup in the Virgin Islands. "Your new girl is my clone."

On "Now That We Don’t Talk," she references the doomed vacation again, and slams Harry’s infamous music taste in the lines, "I don’t have to pretend I like acid rock / Or that I’d like to be on a mega-yacht."

And while Taylor went on to date several more stars from across the pond, Harry was her first British bloke. And since London is referenced in other songs in her earlier catalogue, including Red’s "Come Back, Be Here" and "Message in a Bottle," the tracks are also speculated to be about Harry.

Harry didn’t earn the entirety of 1989’s inspiration. Indeed, many fans believe the track "Bad Blood" is about Katy as Taylor teased to Rolling Stone in 2014 it was about another "female artist," who "tried to sabotage an entire arena tour."

"I was like, 'Oh, we’re just straight-up enemies,'" Taylor, who at the time saw some of her background dancers leave for Katy's Prismatic tour, added. "It wasn’t even about a guy! It had to do with business."

However, Taylor maintained she penned the song simply to get some feelings off her chest.

"My intent was not to create some gossip-fest," she added to Rolling Stone. "I wanted people to apply it to a situation where they felt betrayed in their own lives."

Ultimately, though, the song fueled a feud—with Katy posting on X one day after the Rolling Stone piece published, "Watch out for Regina George in sheep’s clothing."

The singers were later able to squash their beef in 2019, after which Katy made a cameo in Taylor’s "You Need to Calm Down" music video.

Taylor can write fanfiction, too. Ahead of the release of Red, Taylor met Ethel while dating her grandson Conor Kennedy, and ultimately penned the song "Starlight" about a reimagined version of a date night between the Kennedy matriarch and her late husband.

"Starlight is a song that I wrote after seeing a picture of Ethel and Bobby Kennedy when they were 17," Taylor explained in a Red interview. "I didn’t know anything about what they were doing or what was going on in the picture, but I just thought 'They look like they’re having the best night.' And so I wrote this song about what the night might’ve been like."

In response to the nod, Ethel told the Cape Cod Times, "She is just sensational, inside and out."

One of Taylor’s most popular breakup songs of all time "All Too Well"—and its 10-minute alternate version—is thought to be about the Donnie Darko star. After all, it references autumn—when their short-lived 2010 romance took place—her subject’s sister’s house, and a certain scarf. (Jake, of course, has a very famous sister in Maggie Gyllenhaal, and the duo passed a striped Gucci scarf between them during their romance.)

Taylor also appeared to take shots at her romance with Jake in "The Last Time," "We Are Never Getting Back Together," and the Red vault track "I Bet You Think About Me," which call out the subject’s music taste and wealthy background.

Despite widespread belief Red as a whole was mostly inspired by Jake, he shut down any connection following the album’s 2021 rerelease.

"It’s about her relationship with her fans," he told Esquire in 2022. "It is her expression."

Taylor, meanwhile, did concur with Jake's sentiment, noting that she saw "All Too Well" become something much deeper than a breakup song.

"What was so crazy is that when it went out into the world, the fans just among themselves decided it was their favorite too," she explained on Good Morning America in 2021.  "They just sort of ... claimed it as the most important song from Red...over the course of the first six months the album was out."

Many fans speculate that The Tortured Poets Department's "The Manuscript" is about the impact of "All Too Well," and thus, Taylor's relationship with Jake.

Yes, at least half of Taylor’s heart—at the age of 19, anyway—once belonged to the "Gravity" musician. And it possibly led to some of her Speak Now tracks like "Dear John," and "The Story of Us," which Taylor previously revealed were inspired by the same person.

"'The Story of Us' is about running into someone I had been in a relationship with at an awards show, and we were seated a few seats away from each other," she told USA Today in 2010. "I just wanted to say to him, 'Is this killing you? Because it's killing me.' But I didn't. Because I couldn't. Because we both had these silent shields up."

While Taylor has said she doesn’t use Easter eggs to hint at her personal life, the "Story of Us" liner notes—where Taylor used to hide messages for her fans—on the original Speak Now album spelled out "CMT Awards," an event she and John both attended in 2010.

As for where "Dear John" is concerned? John himself had to respond to the brazen shots fired.

"I didn’t deserve it," the musician told Rolling Stone in 2012. "I'm pretty good at taking accountability now, and I never did anything to deserve that. It was a really lousy thing for her to do."

Once too young to be messed with, Taylor is now too wise to be bothered with any drama. "I don’t care about anything that happened to me when I was 19," she told fans ahead of playing "Dear John," at The Eras Tour in 2023. "Except for the songs that I wrote and the memories we made together."

As she put it, “I do not care. We’ve all grown up. We’re good.”

Following a 2009 romance with the Twilight star, Taylor penned "Back to December" about the relationship. In addition to alluding to a "September night" where her subject saw her cry (Lautner was also at the 2009 VMAs), she included a nod to him in the song’s liner notes, which read, "Tay."

Ahead of Speak Now's rerelease in 2023, the Sharkboy and Lava Girl alum joked about his role in the album’s songs, telling Today at the time, "I feel safe."

Some fans also speculate that "Today Was a Fairytale" and "I Can See You"—the music video he starred in—were about her Valentine’s Day costar as well, as in the latter track, Taylor sings about keeping "everything professional," before a romance ensued.

Believe it or not, Taylor once got butterflies from the "Fireflies" singer. "Enchanted" is about a night she met the frontman for Owl City, and she revealed she included the line "wonderstruck" so he’d know it was about him, as he had used the word in an email to her.

"Meeting him," Taylor told Yahoo in 2010. "It was this overwhelming feeling of: I really hope that you’re not in love with somebody."

A year later, Adam responded to the musical love letter by rerecording the song, adding in his own lyrics, "Oh Taylor, I was so enchanted to meet you too."

"I'll be the first to admit I’m a rather shy boy and since music is the most eloquent form of communication I can muster, I decided to record something for you–a sort of a 'reply' to the breathtaking song on your current record," he added in a note beneath the song, shared to his band's website at the time. "You are a true princess from a dreamy fairy tale."

Once upon a time, Taylor was extremely up front when it came to who inspired her songs, especially where her breakup with Joe Jonas is concerned. Back in 2008, she quickly penned "Forever and Always" and tacked it on as a last-minute addition to Fearless, perfectly timed to her infamous appearance on Ellen, where she called out the Jonas Brothers member for breaking up with her in a 27-second phone call.

On her next album, Speak Now, released in 2010, Taylor included two nods to Joe, including "Last Kiss," a heart-wrenching ballad which references July 9, a.k.a. the date of the 2008 Jonas Brothers concert she attended while she and Joe were still together.

Elsewhere on the album, Taylor included "Better Than Revenge," which was a clap back at the Jonas Brothers’ song "Much Better," which had a not-so-veiled reference to her in the lyric, "I'm done with superstars and all the tears on her guitar."

Later on in her discography, Taylor included fonder nods to her past romance with Joe on Red’s "Holy Ground," and folklore’s "Invisible String," the latter in which she reflects on becoming friendly with him in more recent years. "Cold was the steel of my axe to grind for the boys who broke my heart," she sings in the song, "Now I send their babies presents."

However, when Taylor released Fearless (Taylor’s Version) in 2021, she gave Joe one more whack with "Mr. Perfectly Fine," though she penned the song around the time of their 2008 breakup. It was Joe’s now-ex-wife Sophie Turner who seemingly confirmed the track was about her then-husband, sharing the song to social media at the time and joking, "It's not NOT a bop."

#755. Real Madrid close on agreement to sign Manchester United 16-year-old JJ Gabriel

Madrid hope to bring in forward during January

United to consider legal action if they feel rules broken

Real Madrid are closing in on signing JJ Gabriel, though Manchester United will consider legal action if the club believe any rules have been broken.

Madrid have offered the 16‑year‑old forward a multi‑year contract and, subject to final talks, hope to bring him to the Bernabéu in January. Gabriel is registered with United’s academy until the end of the season and it is understood the club have yet to be contacted by the player’s camp or Real Madrid regarding the proposed move.

Madrid intend to sign Gabriel via a Fifa loophole that allows clubs in the EU to secure young players on professional contracts if they have an EU passport, which Gabriel is eligible to acquire through both his parents.

Fifa would have to sign this off and United are on alert regarding any potential breach of regulations. A compensation fee would be due to United if Gabriel joined Madrid or any other team. Madrid have been approached for comment.

Gabriel walked out on United in September and is believed to be training in Spain. A move to Madrid offers the prospect of progression to senior football via their B team, Castilla, who play in the regionalised Spanish third tier.

Gabriel played in a pre-season friendly for United against Atlético Madrid in Stockholm in August at the age of 15 and had been training with the first team. If he had not informed United of his wish to depart, he would have been in Michael Carrick’s squad for the Carabao Cup third-round defeat against Brighton on 16 September. Had Gabriel featured, he would have become the youngest player in the club’s history.

Last season Gabriel became the youngest winner of United’s academy player of the year award and was the Premier League’s under‑18 player of the season.

#754. Canadian PM Mark Carney discusses talks with the EU, overdependence on the US and how to deal with Donald Trump in a DW interview.

Prime Minister Mark Carney tells DW that Canada is seeking closer EU ties to "diversify and deepen" partnerships beyond the Americas. Despite German pushback, he said he favors the all-new term "associate membership."

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney spoke to DW on Friday after talks in Montreal with European Union leaders seeking to hammer out details of a new, closer partnership between Canada and the EU.

Amid difficult negotiations with US President Donald Trump, representing Canada's biggest trading partner, Carney said that he and his compatriots had come to realize the country was too dependent on the economic powerhouse to the south.

"The lesson we've taken, Canadians as a whole, is we're overdependent on the United States. Too closely connected to the United States. And we need to build our strength here at home and diversify and deepen our partnerships with like-minded countries internationally," Carney said.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

An EU delegation led by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa held talks with Carney and other Canadian officials in Montreal on Friday.

They're discussing the plans floated by Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to forge what she called an "associate membership" — a status that does not yet exist for any other country — even as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's government resists creating this label. Carney seemed to speak in its favor.

"Well, I think the advantage of what we're doing is that a few things are absolutely clear, irrespective of the exact terminology that's used. President von der Leyen uses associated membership. We use associated membership," he told DW's Katharina Kroll at Port of Montreal Tower.

"What does that mean? It means the closest possible partnership without being a full member of the European Union, because Canada is not in Europe geographically and therefore cannot have accession." Carney said.

Asked if he was looking to create a "new transatlantic bloc without the US," Carney said it was more about diversifying and deepening Canada's other partnerships than excluding by far its largest trading partner.

"We're both partners of the United States, obviously close partners, alliance partners in NATO. And there are many, many opportunities for cooperation with the United States," he said. "But in many cases, there'll be much deeper cooperation for Canada between Canada and Europe than Canada and the United States."

He mentioned both existing areas of cooperation like the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), calling it "one of the most successful free trade agreements in the world," and also pointed to research cooperation and programs like Horizon Europe and Erasmus+ enabling student exchanges.

But Carney also pointed to areas where the two sides could seek to expand cooperation, naming areas like space technologies, artificial intelligence and critical minerals.

Despite his well-documented difficulties with Donald Trump — perhaps most crudely exemplified by Trump's attempts to unilaterally rename Lake Ontario, or his posting AI videos imagining him as an ice hockey player beating Carney up in a fight — Carney said US-Canadian ties were too deep to be derailed by any governments or prime ministers or presidents.

"The bonds between Canadians and Americans are longstanding. They're very strong. And big elements of that will be maintained regardless of the government in Canada, the government in the United States, the combination of the two," he said.

Asked about the best way to deal with Trump, Carney said it was "to be direct, to be clear, to be absolutely clear about your bottom lines are." He said it was important to show respect but also to continue to bring "the negotiations back to the core issues."

But he said the tensions with Trump had demonstrated the need to diversify and to seek Canada's other most natural partners around the world.

He acknowledged that no matter the nature of the talks with the EU, "the scale of the relationship with the United States" would be "very hard to replace."

Asked if he was concerned that the talks could expose him to further tariffs or other punitive measures from the Trump administration, Carney said, "We've been living with this for some time."

"There have been many justifications for trade action against Canada that the United States has had," he said. "Our view is that all of them are unjustified under our trade agreement."

Carney said the crucial message, also for the Trump White House, was that the talks with Brussels concerned a "positive association" and partnership "to help solve global problems" and address global challenges.

"It's not against somebody. It's for. It's a positive act," he said.

#753. Why Man Utd's Roma comeback has echoes of Mourinho and Solskjaer

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick (second left) hugs Shea Lacey after the 3-2 Champions League victory against Roma

It was impossible not to get swept up in the emotion and delirium of Manchester United's late 3-2 Champions League comeback win against Roma.

Old Trafford was transformed from a mutinous, baying cathedral of distrust and fury to one of joy and celebration.

Nine games and almost eight weeks is an eternity to wait for a victory at a club of Manchester United's size.

It didn't take Michael Carrick long to calm the mood.

"It's one win, so we're not getting too carried away with things, but it was an important win."

It was a huge result in the sense it bought Carrick some time. But given United's general state, no-one can be sure how much.

And, as was quickly pointed out in the aftermath of the victory, Manchester United have been here before.

Man Utd produce incredible second-half comeback to beat Roma

A half-time speech, a retaken penalty - and a win to save Carrick's job?

Jose Mourinho (centre) was sacked after a 3-1 defeat at Liverpool in December 2018

'Jose Mourinho set to be sacked whatever Manchester United's result vs Newcastle.'

As headlines go, it was attention grabbing.

As it turned out, the Mirror was wrong. Although United officials at the time tried to play down the situation, sources have since admitted the intention was to sack Mourinho after presiding over the club's worst start to a season in 29 years, and defeat by Newcastle would make it inevitable.

Much like the Roma game, the visitors raced into a two-goal lead and the atmosphere in the stadium started to turn, with most of the venom aimed at the director's box rather than the manager.

Mourinho, who had promoted Carrick to assistant coach, replaced Eric Bailly with Juan Mata after 19 minutes and it was Mata who scored the 70th-minute goal that sparked the comeback, completed by Alexis Sanchez in the final minute for a 3-2 victory.

After the game, Mourinho said the pressure on him was a "manhunt". However, the relationship between manager and club had been turning sour since the previous summer. His demand for Anthony Martial to be sold had been rejected, while record signing Paul Pogba was proving a problem.

While the Newcastle win sparked an improvement in form, a run of two wins in eight games culminating in a 3-1 loss at Liverpool led to Mourinho's dismissal 10 weeks later.

Former United defender Rio Ferdinand dismissed calls for Ole Gunnar Solskjaer to be sacked before the Champions League encounter with Atalanta on 20 October 2021 as representative of "current fan culture".

Carrick was also part of Solskjaer's coaching group as United went top of the Premier League when they beat Newcastle just over a month earlier, but two wins in seven suggested all was not well.

As he did with Roma, coach Gian Piero Gasperini saw his team establish a two-goal lead by half-time, then collapse. Cristiano Ronaldo was the matchwinner on this occasion, nine minutes from time for another 3-2 win.

Even if United had lost that night, it is hard to think Solskjaer's job would have been under threat. What followed immediately afterwards was a totally different story.

Liverpool came to Old Trafford and established a four-goal first-half lead. Jurgen Klopp's men won 5-0, their biggest ever away win over their old rivals.

Many United fans thought Solskjaer should go that night. It was three weeks later that it happened, after a 4-1 defeat at Watford.

Man Utd beat Roma - the other great Champions League comebacks

Fernandes critical of media 'lies' about Carrick relationship

Manchester United skipper Bruno Fernandes celebrates Matheus Cunha's winner against Roma

One look at the Premier League table shows why Carrick is right not to get carried away.

If results go against them, Manchester United could be bottom of the table by the time they kick-off against Aston Villa on Sunday.

Neither Mourinho nor Solskjaer could follow up their 3-2 successes with another victory. Mourinho's United drew at Chelsea, then lost at home to Juventus. Solskjaer's United were embarrassed by Liverpool. It meant neither man was able to build on the momentum generated by their epic victories.

United have gone seven Premier League games without a win. They went eight under Ruben Amorim at the end of the 2024-25 campaign, but draws and losses were split by victories en route to the Europa League final, so the effect was not as great as it feels right now.

The club does have an exceptional home record against Villa. They have won their past six in all competitions and lost just two league games against the Midlands outfit at Old Trafford since 1983.

When United sources finally communicated - almost 48 hours after the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on 25 October - that Carrick and his players would be given the opportunity to turn the situation around, no timescale was put on this. However, the feeling was the forthcoming international break would be an appropriate time for the club hierarchy to take stock and decide what direction they should go in.

In the two games since, Carrick's team have been excellent across two halves.

Victory against Villa, albeit with Â£70m Carlos Baleba joining the injured list, would haul them up to within two points of Unai Emery's side heading into a tricky run of matches post international break, starting at Liverpool, but also including trips to Newcastle and Arsenal in December.

Defeat is likely to dump them in the relegation zone for at least a fortnight and facing severe baiting at Anfield on 22 November.

"It's not about me," is a phrase Carrick has repeated often as he has assessed the wreckage of another bad result. The outcome against Roma was much more positive.

There is no suggestion Carrick's future has been decided just yet. What happens at Old Trafford this weekend looks very important.

#751. Bob Dylan, 85, Meets With Pope Leo XIV in Rare Public Appearance

Bob Dylan stepped out for a meeting with Pope Leo XIV on Nov. 4, marking a rare public appearance for the 85-year-old musician.

All along the watchtower, eyes were on the Vatican as Pope Leo XIV (born Robert Francis Prevost) crossed paths with Bob Dylan (born Robert Allen Zimmerman).

After all, Dylan has long been known for knock, knock, knockin’ on Heaven’s door, and this time the way opened up for a private meeting between the head of the Catholic church and the celebrated musician on Nov. 4.

For the occasion, Dylan and Pope Leo’s outfits painted a humorously opposite picture. Where Pope Leo, 71, was a vision in white in a classic cassock, Dylan was dressed in black almost entirely from head to toe, including a jacket he wore with the hood up during the meeting.

As for what exactly the singer and the pontiff pontificated about, Vatican News reported only that the pair swapped greetings and “a few lighthearted exchanges” during the “brief” meeting. The Pope reportedly gave Dylan a rosary, while the singer gave the Catholic leader a copy of his autobiography, Chronicles: Volume One.

Meanwhile, Vatican official Rev. Antonio Spadaro—who helped organize the rendezvous—shared what it was like to witness the meeting.

“It was hard not to feel the emotion of being part of an encounter that had a real sense of history about it,” Spadaro wrote on social media, “with the feeling that, at every step through the Apostolic Palace, absolutely anything could happen!”

But in a world where anything can, in fact, happen, this particular meeting seemed somewhat preordained, with Leo have previously proven his Dylan fandom.

Back in July, the Pope quoted Dylan’s work in Disarmed and Disarming: Peace is a Gift, a book published by the Vatican Publishing House. In the book’s preface, the Pope cited Dylan’s 1963 nuclear protest song “Go Away You Bomb.”

Specifically, Leo recalled the line, “I hate you cause yer man-made and man-owned, an’ man-handled.”

The American-born Leo, however, is not the first Pope into whose orbit the wind has blown Dylan, 85.

In fact, back in 1997, the singer-songwriter performed for Pope John Paul II at the 23rd National Eucharistic Congress in Bologna, Italy.

John Paul, too, looked to Dylan’s lyrics to inspire, quoting from his song “Blowin’ in the Wind” in an address to the crowd of 30,000 that was at the event.

“You ask me, ‘How many roads must a man walk down / before you can call him a man?’” the Pope asked, adding, “Only one. There is only one road for man, and that is the road of Jesus Christ.”

#750. Championship roundup: West Ham stage dramatic comeback on Scott Parker’s opening night

West Ham recover from 3-0 down to draw 3-3 at Cardiff

Leaders Middlesbrough beaten 2-0 at Wrexham

Scott Parker’s return to West Ham had had looked like beginning in painful fashion but instead featured a stunning comeback from 3-0 down. The east London club’s new head coach had watched Cardiff’s Jack Moylan score a first-half hat-trick, before a rousing response after the break ended with Max Kilman levelling the scores at 3-3 eight minutes from time. Elsewhere in the Championship, the leaders Middlesbrough went down 2-0 at Wrexham.

Parker had been confirmed as West Ham’s head coach earlier on Wednesday, taking over from Nuno Espírito Santo, who was sacked on Tuesday. The club’s former midfielder was appointed on a two-and-a-half-year contract.

Moylan halted the initial feelgood factor among the visiting support in the 11th minute at Cardiff City Stadium. His right-foot drive from the tip of the D left the visiting goalkeeper Mads Hermansen helpless as it sped into the top left corner. Moylan was then brought down for a penalty – the Ireland midfielder got up to spank it home to the left as Hermansen dived right in the 37th minute.

Within two minutes, Will Fish thought he had turned in a corner for Cardiff’s third – the centre-back deftly headed towards goal, but Moylan was directly behind him and claimed his hat-trick after making the final touch.

After the break, it was a completely different story. Divine Mukasa reduced the deficit in the 58th minute, finishing calmly over the stranded Nathan Trott after a fine ball over the top from Jarrod Bowen, before Arne Engels capitalised on a mix-up in the home defence to make it 3-2.

In the 82nd minute, Bowen was again the supplier, curling in an inviting cross from the right that was turned in by the centre-back Kilman to make it 3-3 from close range.

At the Racecourse, Wrexham waited until the 70th minute to break the deadlock against Middlesbrough, before George Thomason smashed a shot into the ground from just outside the area, which rocketed past a crowd of defenders and through the unsighted visiting goalkeeper Radek Vítek. Oli Rathbone then made it 2-0 in the 84th minute.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Scott Twine scored a stunning, curling free-kick to give Bristol City the lead at Ashton Gate but the promotion-chasing Wolves turned the match around with two late goals from Sean Neave to make it a 2-1 win to the visitors. Neave, on loan from Newcastle, came off the bench to score on 82 and 89 minutes to win it for the visitors.

#747. Champions League: Como clobber Lens 9-1 after Real Madrid roar back to deny AEK Athens

Valverde hits late winner as Madrid win 3-2 in Athens

Napoli thrashed by Porto, Club Brugge win at PSV

Anastasios Douvikas led the rout with a hat-trick as Como cruised to a 9-1 victory away at Lens, equalling the record for the most goals scored in a single Champions League game.

Only two teams had previously won a game by a margin of eight goals since the launch of the modern Champions League in 1992.

Liverpool thumped Besiktas 8-0 in the group stage in 2007 and Real Madrid won by the same scoreline against Malmo in 2015.

Como are just the second team to score nine times in a game in the competition, after Bayern Munich beat Dinamo Zagreb 9-2 in the league phase in 2024.

Cesc Fabregas’s side made it three wins from four in their maiden campaign in the competition with a spellbinding display.

Nico Paz continued his fine form with a goal and two assists, while Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martin Baturina and Matteo Papaccioli also scored for the Serie A side, who had already beaten both RB Leipzig and Manchester United 4-1 at home in this campaign.

The last club to score nine away from home in the European Cup was Feyenoord against Olympiakos in 1971.

Federico Valverde lashed home a stunning effort from distance to snatch Real Madrid a late 3-2 victory at AEK Athens on Wednesday and preserve their 100% start in the group phase.

José Mourinho’s side, who started with Vinícius Júnior on the left flank after he missed the team’s previous two La Liga matches through suspension, twice came from behind against the Greek champions before Valverde claimed all three points for his side.

Aboubakary Koïta sent AEK ahead after 12 minutes before Jude Bellingham equalised with a sublime flick for the record 15-time winners.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Stavros Pilios sent the Greek champions ahead with 15 minutes to go but Kylian Mbappé swiftly pulled Madrid level once again, setting the stage for Valverde’s late winner.

Madrid have now won seven straight games across all competitions.

Scott McTominay found the net but Napoli suffered a 4-1 defeat by Porto, who had lost their first three games in the competition, while Club Brugge are up to ninth after a 2-1 win at PSV.

Konstantinos Karetsas struck a 72nd-minute winner as Borussia Dortmund beat Real Betis 2-1 while Erik Botheim helped himself to two goals as Viking secured their first triumph with a 4-1 win over 10-man Sabah.

#746. Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like

What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

As a child growing up in Australia, Louise Pain hated her surname.

"People used to tease me; I was called things like 'Pain in the a*s,'" she told DW. "I remember actively hating my surname when I was a child and wanting to change it."

The jokes have followed her throughout her life, even after she moved to Germany. But one thing did eventually change: Pain's feelings about her own name.

Names are not only a fundamental part of how we identify ourselves — they can, beyond teasing, also influence how other people treat us. So, what happens if we dislike our own name, or if it is perceived negatively by those around us?

"A person's name is vital to their sense of identity," psychoanalyst Mikita Brottman told DW. "When someone has an embarrassing name, that embarrassment can be incorporated into their identity."

Research on name bias has linked negatively perceived names with romantic rejection,as well as lower educational outcomes, lower self-esteem and more frequent smoking.

This suggests that names could influence our life trajectory, namely through self-esteem and opportunity.

But a person's relationship with their name is not necessarily fixed. Pain's lived experience, and that of another woman with the first name Tiny, shows how people can find ways to reclaim, and even come to value, names that once triggered ridicule and rejection.

Names can act as "signals" when you first meet someone, personality psychologist Jochen Gebauer told DW. Those signals may lose importance as people get to know each other, but Gebauer said their effects could also accumulate over a lifetime, potentially contributing to "real measurable advantages and disadvantages."

Research led by sociologist Anthony Lee found that a name can evoke inaccurate assumptions about intelligence, competence, trustworthiness, sociability and attractiveness. For Pain, other people's reactions have extended beyond jokes. In high school, a teacher refused to believe that 'Pain' was her real surname and reprimanded her in front of the class.

"Your name couldn't possibly be Pain. Write your real name!" she recalled the teacher saying.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

In Lee's UK-based research, less familiar names tended to fall along a dimension partly characterized as "weirdness," which may help explain why difficult-to-pronounce or culturally unfamiliar names receive more negative evaluations.

Tiny, now 54, encountered the same questions about her unfamiliar name growing up in Greece.

Her parents had adapted "Tiny" to "Tinie" to make it sound more Greek, but people would repeatedly ask what her real or baptismal name was.

Even relatives have refused to accept it. Recently, two elderly aunts introduced her to someone as "Haritini," a conventional Greek name.

"I didn't even bother correcting them at this point," Tiny told DW.

Tiny's relationship with her name has also evolved.

"The jokes [from others] got repetitive and boring pretty fast, so at least I was left with the sense that I have something unique with my name going on."

Pain, now 40, discovered how much cultural context could change the reaction to her surname when she began learning her father's native French as a teenager. In French, 'pain' means bread.

"People started calling me 'Bread! Louise Bread.'"

Later, after moving to Germany, the jokes became mostly bread-related rather than the more scathing ones she had experienced in Australia. "That helped me to feel better about my name," she said.

As they got older, both Pain and Tiny developed coping strategies to pre-empt people's reactions to their names.

Tiny sometimes introduces herself with: "Hi, I'm Tiny. It's my name and not a statement," or, "I'm Tiny. Not a difficult name to live up to."

"This usually stops people from asking awkward questions."

Pain also began to embrace the humor surrounding her name.

"I was convinced that I should become either a doctor or a dominatrix, or perhaps both, to become either 'Doctor Pain,' or 'Mistress Pain.'"

"Names can conjure that whole spectrum of shame and pride," psychoanalyst Melissa Daum told DW.

Pain now finds that people tend to see her surname as "funny and endearing… it's become something that is more of a funny talking point."

But the childhood discomfort has not entirely disappeared. When Pain thinks about having children, her feelings about the name become more complicated.

"I don't really want to pass on my surname ... so there is a deeper wound there."

But Pain also believes her father would be deeply hurt if future children had a different name. The surname she once hated connects her to him and to her French heritage.

"Something that once feels like an inconvenience or a source of self-consciousness can become a marker of distinctiveness, history, or belonging," Daum said.

"My parents seemingly made an unfortunate choice, but by now I have embraced both the name and the sense of uniqueness that comes with it."

That does not mean she uses Tiny everywhere. She avoids it on dating apps because "Tiny might give off the wrong message," and does not use it in her email address when she wants to appear professional.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Pain, meanwhile, uses a Germanized version of the French word for bread as her social media surname.

Online, people have more control over what name they present to others. As Daum put it: "Choosing one's own name can feel like an act of mastery, even a refusal of that original passivity: I will decide what I am called and how I am encountered."

But accepting a name does not necessarily mean embracing it in every situation.

Pain once wanted to change her surname. Tiny considered using her middle name in her thirties. Neither ultimately abandoned the names that had caused them difficulties.

For Tiny, at least, a name that once made her feel awkward has become something she can imagine carrying for the rest of her life.

"It might be cute to eventually be a granny called Tiny."

#744. 14 Gifts the New York City Girl in Your Life Will Actually Want

Whether she’s commuting, exploring, or getting ready for a night out, these thoughtful picks fit right into her busy city life.

Whether you also live in the city or you have a long-distance bestie, gift shopping for the New York City girl in your life can feel impossible. They probably have it all, and if they don’t, they live in the best place to get it in person. Unless you get a FaceTime haul every time they shop, you probably have a slim chance to get the perfect gift for them.

It can be hard to be tapped into the NYC lifestyle enough to know what they want (before they even know they want it). Luckily, I got you. While I wasn’t born and raised in New York, I have been living here for five years now. And as a shopping writer, I’ve tried plenty of products throughout the year to be able to tell you what the average NYC girl would want to get under the tree this year.

When in doubt, opt for gifts that have a sleek city vibe, are practical for on-the-go, and actually work. We recommend starting with a chic pouch (or tin can) that you can customize with their name, and filling it with luxury skincare, hair, makeup, and fragrance minis. Then, choose a good-quality item based on their vibe—whether it’s a wool coat, a screenless digital camera, or a shoulder bag.

So, keep scrolling to shop for the best gifts for the NYC girl in your life, according to this NYC writer.

Available in new limited-edition holiday shades, this gorgeous lip gloss serum is infused with hyaluronic acid, squalane, and castor oil to leave your lips soft, shiny, and lightly tinted. Plus, it comes in a convenient (and chic) tin that fits in every mini bag you need while you’re out in the city.

Looking for custom embroidery? Abbode is an iconic spot in SoHo to get just that. There are so many options to choose from, but my heart was captured by this sleek and stylish croc pouch that you can customize with their signature or a phrase and decorate with a cute icon. Imagine gifting them this with lots of chic minis inside? Obsessed.

Created by celebrity makeup artist Mary Phillips, the m.ph brand is that line in Sephora everyone wishes they had in their collection. With its sleek packaging and amazing formulas, it’s practically made for the city girl. If you don’t have their specific shade for the new foundation, we recommend the viral underpainting palette that started it all.

Whether your NYC bestie loves to host or needs a cheeky drink before bed, these martini glasses are perfect for their home with their custom name engraved in a variety of font options.

Looking for a film-type camera without the hassle of going somewhere to develop it, but still want to have an air of mystery of how the photos turned out? The Camp Snap screenless digital camera is exactly that. It’s lightweight enough to throw in your bag, and has four film-style modes with a built-in memory that’s incredibly fun to play around.

Outside In’s flagship store recently opened in the LES, with a full coffee bar, lovely garden backyard, a fragrance gallery, a makeup section, and a Nature of Things spa-like section. If you’re looking to gift something from this brand, I recommend the mascara, with its skinny “cig-like” and luxe silver packaging and formula full of tubing technology, shea butter, vegan waxes, and more.

This winter, you don’t have to put away all of your ballet flats. Legwarmers will be all over the city this season, so get these faux fur ones from Urban Outfitters that feature a chic neutral colorway and fuzzy texture.

Whether they’re waiting for their next train underground or touching up in the Uber, every city girl needs a luxe hairbrush (or two) while they’re on the go. La Bonne Brosse is simply that brand. This set includes a small version of their iconic boar bristle brush and a wide-tooth comb in a matching lovely pink colorway.

In my NYC closet, there can never be too many sneakers—especially when they’re a trendy chocolate shade, low-profile, and extremely comfortable for walking around for hours. Extra points if they’re a K-Pop (and Blackpink) fan, because these new Puma x Rosé sneakers are a perfect gift.

You can also never have too many bags! This Kate Spade shoulder bag is delicate and practical for city living (and absolutely gorgeous in person), with its icy lavender shade, suede texture, silver hardware, 3D flower details, and adjustable shoulder strap.

Every NYC girl needs a good cleansing routine for when she gets home after a whole day out in the city. Make that routine better with this gift set that includes these bestselling ELEMIS cleansing balms and soft cleansing cuffs.

Every city girl needs a good facial, and this skincare device gives the most relaxing one right at home. Mount Lai’s Gua Sha device features a 660nm red LED light, up to 113F degree heat therapy, and white jade rollers that’ll leave your skin smooth and sculpted.

Your bestie might have a whole fragrance collection, but does she have luxury scents in chic mini sizes? Not only are they adorable, but they’re also so handy for all on-the-go it girls. This fragrance set from Maison Francis Kurkdjian features five of the brand’s top-rated scents in small glass vials.

When it comes to gifting coats and sweaters to your friend who lives in New York, opt for one that has 100% (or a majority) natural fibers that’ll actually keep them warm this season. This Madewell coat is 100% wool and features a relaxed fit, a convertible funnel-neck collar, dolman sleeves, and cozy welt pockets.

#742. Kim Kardashian Reveals She Eats "Prop Food" on All's Fair Set

Kim Kardashian admitted she often eats the prop food on the set of Hulu's All's Fair, costarring Sarah Paulson, Glenn Close, Niecy Nash-Betts, Teyana Taylor and Naomi Watts.

For Kim Kardashian, all's fair on the set of All's Fair.

That's why she has no problem eating prop food while filming scenes with costars Sarah Paulson, Niecy Nash-Betts, Naomi Watts, Glenn Close and Teyana Taylor for their Hulu legal drama.

"It's real food and I eat it the whole time," Kardashian said during the cast's Nov. 4 appearance on Good Morning America. "I'll be walking by after they cut and I'm like, 'Can I take a plate of that pie with me?'"

And her castmates have objections to her unusual snacking habit. As Nash-Betts quipped, "Do not let that tiny body fool you: She eats everything."

"I said, 'This is prop food! Why are you eating this?'" she continued with a laugh. "This is the greediest woman I've ever met in my life."

But there's a reason why Kardashian's costars have dismissed prop food.

"We don't want to eat it all day," Paulson explained, with Watts adding, "It's a thing called continuity. If you eat it in the scene, you have to keep doing it."

However, their testimonies haven't swayed Kardashian one bit.

"Because I'm new to this, they tried to tell me, 'Hey, continuity. Pace yourself. Eat a grape or half a grape because you're gonna have to do that the same time 50 times,'" the 46-year-old shared. "By the end, I am like, 'What did I get myself into?' But I love it."

In fact, the Keeping Up With the Kardashians alum has even recreated some of her own snacks with Rice Krispies off set. As she put it, "Last night in my room, I made Rice Krispie treats because I wanted all the girls to try them."

And while the jury's still out on Kardashian as a cook, her costars have been thoroughly impressed by her acting skills.

"Her ability to remember her lines, she's so good with that," Taylor raved to E! News last year. "She'll keep reading it over and over and over again. It's dope to see."

Added Close, "She's a very sweet woman, she does her homework, she has great people around her, which says a lot."

To find out what other stars are snacking on these days, read on...

"Fruit and raw nuts. Recently I've made an effort to keep lost of fresh products and nuts on hand for snacking in-between meals."

"I am snacking so much while I've been at home! I think it's because I'm home and near my fridge all day. I slice up an apple and it fills me up between meals. I love the satisfying crunch and so do my kids."

"My go-to snack is canned oysters. I know that might sound weird, but I am absolutely obsessed with canned oysters. They are such a good source of protein, magnesium and vitamin C. They are so tasty and always fill me up. I eat them straight out of the can, but sometimes if I want some extra carbs, I'll eat them with crackers and the crunch of the cracker with the soft oyster is so good!"

"Carrots and hummus is always a fave with a handful of raw almonds and/or cashews."

"I always have a cup of fruit near me, usually with grapes or berries. For drinks, I like homemade green juice. I mix in BODYARMOR Lyte, Coconut for some sweetness and flavor without having to worry about sugar."

"Handfuls of roasted, unsalted almonds, a slice of sourdough bread with cashew butter and sliced bananas, a smoothie (mine usually have whole milk Greek yogurt, ice, a handful of spinach, some pineapple, whatever milk I have (right now it is Forager Coconut Cashew Oat), a banana, half an avocado, two dates, a dash of cinnamon (and sometimes a scoop of nut butter)."

"Hot Cheetos and fruit with tajin and lemon, yummy!"

"Fruit! I can't think of a more perfect food."

"Cheese and crackers with lots of cheese."

"Avocado with salt. It's the right amount of indulgent with being super easy to make. If I have more time I'll add a poached egg with a smidge of hot sauce from Big Reds."

"Apples and peanut butter but not just your average apples and peanut butter, folks. There is a science to this special snack. First, they have to be honeycrisp apples, cut very thin. Then you get your peanut butter, melt it, add some honey and stir all the deliciousness together! This creates almost like a caramel consistency. You don't use nearly as much peanut butter and you avoid getting it on your thumb every time you dip. Brilliant, I know!"

"Popcorn because I love the salt. But I don't feel terrible after I eat it because popcorn is pretty light!"

"My go-to snack at the moment is going to sound so strange: I like to take a flour tortilla with salted butter melted in a pan and then I top it with Nutella. I know it's weird! LOL, it's honestly like an easier version of a crêpe and that's why I love it."

"Prosciutto and mozzarella cheese is my favorite snack, I have it almost every day."

"Half an avocado with a drizzle of olive oil, squeeze of lemon and a dash of truffle salt. Extremely satisfying."

"I wish I could say it was something healthy but I'm a child at heart and it's by far Flavor Blasted Goldfish. LOL!"

#741. Erling Haaland settles thriller for Manchester City to end RB Leipzig resistance

Feed Erling Haaland and Manchester City’s totemic No 9 will score. The problem, recently, has been a paucity of openings for him.

This was true again before Elliot Anderson crossed and Haaland slid home a priceless winner for Enzo Maresca’s disjointed unit, Rayan Cherki hitting a post late on.

The win ends City’s sequence of two losses in three games yet the manager has major issues. He has to plug a leaky defence and drill his midfield to exert control.

And there is a shaky Gianluigi Donnarumma: City’s goalkeeper was culpable for Ridle Baku’s first equaliser for Leipzig, as he was for Nicolas Jackson’s winner in the recent defeat at Aston Villa, plus two more in last month’s Paris Saint-Germain loss.

The manager said: “It’s not a concern but it’s a mistake. But in 48 hours [Saturday] we have Nottingham Forest away, we need to be focused on that and then in the international break I will look. At the moment I’m not thinking about the goalkeeping situation. Gigio knows he was not good with the first goal.”

He was honest, too, about Antonio Nusa’s second for Leipzig, the forward taking advantage of a lax rearguard. “Both goals are quite silly goals we can avoid,” said Maresca.

Still, after going down to Villa and Brighton in the Premier League, the win is a certifiable tonic ahead of the Forest trip.

City’s quest to return to victorious ways featured an XI of four changes from Saturday’s Brighton reverse. Noteworthy was Maresca’s dropping of Rúben Dias as Abdukodir Khusanov’s pace was preferred at centre-back to the captain, Haaland taking the armband.

While the 2,000-plus travelling support were stationed in a quadrant to the right of Donnarumma’s goal, the noise came from the congregation behind Maarten Vandevoordt’s where a sea of red and white bounced to the tempo of a booming drum. They could roar particularly loud when Nusa flitted across City’s D and unloaded and what should have been a regulation save for Donnarumma became a fumble – and corner for Leipzig.

As can be with this Maresca unit, control was difficult to find and administer for any prolonged passage: Phil Foden twice lost the ball when turning into traffic was no aid, the second time meaning Nusa could zigzag towards goal.

The Brighton defeat featured close to zero service for Haaland and City’s 13-goal man was again hard to find, Matheus Nunes’ loose cross, when the captain lurked, emblematic. So, too, as a sign of Leipzig’s ascendancy, was Marc Guéhi scrambling to clear danger, Nusa firing in the ball from the left, and Christoph Baumgartner having space to shoot marginally wide of Donnarumma’s left post.

“Keep the ball and shift it faster” might have been Maresca’s instruction and when this happened City fashioned the breakthrough.

Cherki speared a diagonal right-left into a galloping Nico O’Reilly, whose instant cross caused Castello Lukeba to panic and turn home, via a trailing left knee. City had forced the issue and twice went close to a second moments later.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

First, O’Reilly floated the ball into Leipzig’s area but Haaland’s header faltered. Then the left-back was set up by Iliman Ndiaye’s cross only for O’Reilly to miss with the same part of his anatomy.

Yet as the second half began Leipzig were staring at a fifth defeat in the fixture, having won only once in six previous meetings, all in this competition.

Intent was signalled by Nusa’s mazy run along the left, his chip causing Donnarumma to push away when he might have caught. This roused the home fans and better followed for their team – but not Donnarumma.

Anderson’s loose ball for O’Reilly near halfway was snaffled by Leipzig, who marauded down the right before Brajan Gruda fed an overlapping Baku. Now, came Donnarumma’s folly because, while the right-back’s shot was true, it was steered along a very tight angle, yet City’s No 1 allowed it to go in between him and his left post.

Here was the latest goal-costing error from the Italian – one for Maresca to ponder. Yet 1-1 was still a fair result away from the Etihad Stadium so relief emanated from those in black when Ezechiel Banzuzi’s shot hit side-netting only. Donnarumma’s wobble continued, though, as he fumbled another Baku attempt, narrowly recovering.

City were about to show character and quality: Ndiaye’s pinpoint cross from the left had Enzo Fernández arriving to head in supremely and Maresca’s team led again. Not for long. Leipzig waltzed through with ease and with Nunes out of position, Nusa finished expertly from the left.

After Anderson skied over from close-range, Haaland did what makes him so lethal: net his sole chance. “Not sure how many touches I had, but most important is that I managed to help the team to win,” said the Norwegian.

#739. AI agents run this automated biology lab that sequences DNA and more

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Heidi Ledford reports for Nature from Seattle, Washington.

A self-driving lab named AutoDNA can work out the constituent ‘letters’ in a snippet of DNA.Credit: Turtle Rock Scientific/Science Source/Science Photo Library

To say that someone has ‘good hands’ is high praise in a molecular biology laboratory, where researchers must deftly handle delicate glassware, pipette samples and more. But in an unusual genetics lab at Shanghai Jiao Tong University in China, a team of robots driven by artificial intelligence is designing and doing experiments with no hands to speak of.

The facility, described today1 in Nature, is one of the latest steps towards ‘self-driving’ labs that are guided by AI, with minimal input from human scientists. With samples moved around by robotic arms, the Shanghai lab can operate more than 20 types of instrument, complete thousands of operations in a single project and do experiments that involve synthesizing and sequencing DNA, among other tasks.

An experiment is designed and executed from start to finish by a team of AI agents, following a simple prompt from a human operator. After that, human hands are needed only to refresh reagents and to service hardware.

The system, called AutoDNA, is remarkable both for its degree of autonomy and because it can readily incorporate a diverse range of lab equipment, says Milad Abolhasani, a chemical engineer at North Carolina State University in Raleigh. “The future of science is going to involve a lot of autonomous labs.”

Labs have long incorporated automation into their workflows, using machines to conduct specific aspects of experimental protocols, such as mixing and heating chemicals. Now, some researchers are hoping to harness increasingly sophisticated AI tools to create self-driving labs, in which an AI system designs and executes complex experiments, troubleshoots and tweaks protocols, and orchestrates activities across an entire lab that is chock-full of disparate equipment.

Designing such labs for molecular biology is challenging because of the field’s complex workflows, which require assorted equipment and high precision, says Haibo Chen, a computer scientist at Shanghai Jiao Tong University and a co-author of the report. “In many existing systems, human experts are still required to configure the instruments,” he says. “AI is mostly added to handle just one part of the process.”

To create a more fully autonomous lab, Chen and his colleagues decided to construct it from the start with AI in mind, rather than adding AI capabilities to a pre-existing system.

The team tested AutoDNA by tasking it with a variety of projects, including detecting a cancer-linked mutation in a sample of DNA. In another experiment, the researchers asked the system to encode a message in DNA using its four nucleotide bases, abbreviated as A, C, G and T. They selected a popular quote, often misattributed to cosmologist Stephen Hawking: “Intelligence is the ability to adapt to change.”

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03552-8

#738. Martha Stewart Blames Craig Melvin for Her Homeless Halloween Costume

Martha Stewart touched on the topic of her controversial Halloween costume, explaining that her appearance alongside Craig Melvin on Today accidentally caused the costume.

Martha Stewart didn’t mean to cause a stir.

Days after the lifestyle guru received backlash for posting a photo of herself dressed as a homeless person for Halloween, she explained her thought process behind the costume, claiming it was the result of Today host Craig Melvin accidentally getting chocolate on her during the show’s Oct. 30 episode.

“He spilled chocolate all over my white sweater, which I was gonna wear on Halloween night,” Stewart said at the CrossCountry Mortgage Sales Rally in Orlando Nov. 3, per footage obtained by TMZ. “When I picked up the sweater, I said, ‘Oh god, it’s so dirty. I only have 10 minutes to get dressed for this Halloween party.’”

“So the easiest costume was to get dressed up as a bum,” the 85-year-old continued. “I looked at myself and I said, ‘You really look hungry and homeless,’ so I wrote a sign that said, ‘I’m hungry.’ And boy, did that go off.”

E! News has reached out to Melvin’s reps for comment but has not heard back.

On the Halloween episode of Today, Stewart led a cooking demonstration in a recreation of her 2026 Winter Olympics look, while Melvin dressed as her longtime friend Snoop Dogg. As Melvin reached for the chocolate ganache, he accidentally spilled some on Stewart.

“Real Snoop would never do that,” she playfully chided, to which Melvin quickly replied, “So sorry, Martha.”

Amid criticism over Stewart’s Halloween costume—which included a beanie, ragged jeans and a plaid button-up under a torn cardigan with dirt smeared across her face—the cookbook author deleted the photo from Instagram and expressed remorse for causing controversy.

“I’ve spent decades teaching others how to celebrate Halloween,”  she said in a statement to People on Nov. 1, “sharing fun, festive recipes, providing unique craft ideas and giving tips on entertaining and hosting to make the most of one of my favorite holidays of the year.”

“I am distressed that my Halloween costume yesterday, which was intended to bring more awareness to the very serious subject of homelessness, has offended people,” she continued, “which was never my intention.”

The TV personality also issued another apology on Instagram, which has since been deleted.

“It’s hard to admit when you’ve really screwed up,” she wrote, per Entertainment Weekly. “My earlier statement didn’t go far enough. I know many people are suffering economically. Wearing a costume like I did was insensitive and not funny. I am very sorry.”

For a look at more of Stewart’s shocking confessions over the years, keep reading.

Martha Stewart—then still Martha Kostyra—lost her virginity when she was 19, to her future husband Andrew Stewart, a student at Yale Law School.

“He was very aggressive,” the lifestyle mogul said in the 2024 Netflix documentary Martha, “and I liked it.”

Martha Stewart Kissed Another Man—on Her Honeymoon

It wasn’t a harbinger of good things to come, but Martha maintained that kissing another man while she and Andrew were honeymooning in Europe after their 1961 nuptials wasn’t that big a deal.

“It was neither naughty nor unfaithful,” she said in Martha of smooching the stranger at a cathedral on Easter eve in Florence, Italy. “It was just emotional, of the moment. That’s how I looked at it. And it was exciting. I wish we could all experience such an evening.”

Martha Stewart Cheated on Husband Andrew Stewart

Martha admitted in the documentary to a “very brief affair” with “a very attractive Irish man” during her time working as a stockbroker in the late 1960s.

“I would have never broken up a marriage for it,” she said. “It was nothing. It was like the kiss in the cathedral.”

She insinuated that Andrew was repeatedly unfaithful, despite her ex-husband maintaining he didn’t cheat until she confessed her infidelity.

“I didn’t go run off with people. He was running off with people,” she said. “I always said I was a swan and like all swans, they are monogamous.”

Being a Mom Wasn’t a Natural Fit for Martha Stewart

Martha had to work at honing her maternal instincts when her daughter Alexis Stewart was born in 1965.

“Back then, everybody was having babies so young,” she reflected in Martha. “That was sort of the style and the habit. I thought it was a natural thing, and it turns out it’s not at all nature to be a mother.”

While she and Alexis remain close, Martha told People in 2020, “I tried to involve her in everything, but the minute she could leave home and go to boarding school, she did. Our relationship has always been a difficult mother-daughter relationship. Difficult, but she would do anything for me, and I would do anything for her."

Martha infamously served five months at FPC Alderson after being convicted in 2004 of conspiracy, obstruction and lying to federal investigators in connection with an insider trading case.

At one point she was punished for touching a female guard’s “big silver key chain” after complimenting how nice the guard looked, as she shared in Martha, having momentarily forgotten the prison rules.

She ended up “dragged into solitary for ‘touching an officer,’” Martha said. “No food or water for a day. This was ‘Camp Cupcake,’ remember?”

Martha Stewart’s Thoughts on Hosting a Talk Show

Upon her release in March 2005, as Martha put it in the doc, she “had to climb out of a f--king hole”—and daytime TV seemed like a step in that direction.

But while she’s been the face of countless endeavors over the years, onscreen and off, hosting Martha for seven seasons, she said, “was more like prison than being at Alderson.”

Martha said on a February 2024 episode of her eponymous podcast that she never had a facelift, but her dermatologist Dr. Daniel Belkin did inject Botox in her neck and along her jawline and put filler in her cheeks and jawline.

Belkin noted that they had also done ultrasound-based skin tightening, and she recalled having a Fraxel laser treatment on her body.

"My décolletage and across my chest looks so good now," Martha told the doctor. "That is a combination of your work and Pilates." She further chalked up her radiant visage to clean eating—her daily green juice ingredients come straight from her garden, naturally—and staying active.

Martha Stewart Enjoys Snoop Dogg’s Contact High

While she didn’t partake herself, Martha felt “fabulous” when her friend and frequent cohost Snoop Dogg smoked weed around her, she shared when he was a guest on the 2022 premiere of her podcast.

“It makes me feel really good," she confessed. "It does not disturb my concentration. In fact, I think it makes it even better and it doesn't make me tired or any of the things people say marijuana does to you. It's fantastic, I think it's great."

The Alcohol Martha Stewart Hadn’t Tasted Since College

Martha loves a craft cocktail, but there’s one spirit that has haunted her since she was a student at Barnard.

“I got so drunk on gin in college,” she told Snoop in 2024 at Food Network's New York City Wine & Food Festival, “that I have not ever had gin since.”

"But," she told her friend, who inevitably entered the alcohol market with the drink he's been linked to for 30 years, "I can’t wait to taste your Gin & Juice!”

Incidentally, though Martha is practically synonymous with white wine, she is not a day drinker.

“I never drink it before dinner, ever," she told The Cut in 2017. "I couldn't function for a second if I had to drink it at lunchtime or something like that."

Why Martha Stewart Doesn’t Wear Underwear

Martha skips wearing underwear in lieu of having her swimsuit on at all times—just in case she feels like taking a dip.

"Bathing suits are my underwear," the 2023 Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue cover girl told Page Six in 2024. "I don't wear any of that structured stuff. No tight lace. I don't wear those. I only wear Eres bathing suits under my clothes."

Martha Stewart’s One-Night Stand Confession

On Watch What Happens Live! in 2013, the answer was “yes” when Andy Cohen asked if Martha ever had a one-night stand. She had also sexted, FYI, and her answer to whether she’d ever had a threesome was a smirking “maybe.”
