#737. Germany's Gen Z protests disrupted by violence on Saturday

Nationwide protests led by young people were largely peaceful throughout the day, but reports about looting and rioting in the evening, especially in Frankfurt, overshadowed the spirit of the demonstrations.

This is a round-up of events at the youth protests across Germany on October 31 and November 1, 2026.

The Gen Z protests in Germany were mostly peaceful throughout the day, with tens of thousands of people having participated across big and smaller cities.

The peaceful demonstrations were overshadowed by reports about violence in some cities like Frankfurt (see below).

Hesse's state interior minister said he suspects that about 100 left-wing extremists instigated the violence in Frankurt.

There were instances of disturbances in Cologne, Hamburg and Bremen, too.

Riots, looting and attacks on police broke out in several German cities after protests by tens of thousands of young people across the country demanding better schools, relief from rising living costs and greater social justice.

The demonstrations had been largely peaceful during the day.

But serious disturbances erupted in the evening in several places.

Clashes broke out in Cologne on Saturday, with about 200 people involved in disturbances near Cologne Cathedral.

Police officers were attacked on the square outside the famous cathedral, with bottles and bicycles hurled toward them.

In a nearby side street, a window was smashed by an electric scooter thrown during the unrest, police said.

According to regional broadcaster WDR, other groups besides Gen Z demonstrators were involved in riots.

Cologne's police chief Johannes Hermanns said it was deeply saddening that peaceful protests were overshadowed by "extremists who had nothing but violence in mind."

While Gen Z protests across Germany were largely peaceful during the day, clashes were reported in several cities as night fell.

German police sealed off a major shopping street in central Frankfurt on Saturday night after rioters smashed shop windows, looted stores and attacked officers following a demonstration.

Police closed Die Zeil, one of Germany's busiest shopping streets, to incoming visitors and urged bystanders to leave the area.

"Anyone not involved who is still on the Zeil can leave. Access to the Zeil is no longer possible," Frankfurt police said in a post on X and in loudspeaker announcements.

Chaotic scenes unfolded along the shopping street, where dpa journalists witnessed people breaking into stores and stealing trainers and other goods.

A specialist firearms shop was also targeted, prompting several arrests, a police spokesman said.

Police also reported attacks on officers, including attacks involving incendiary devices.

The violence erupted after police broke up a demonstration organized as part of the nationwide "Gen Z regelt" (roughly meaning "Gen Z takes charge") protests.

A large contingent of officers was deployed around the Zeil, with authorities advising people to avoid the area or leave central Frankfurt.

The German protests on Saturday are a part of a wider trend that has seen members of Gen Z, born between 1997 and 2012, protest in several European nations.

The wave of protest was triggered by students seeking education reform in France, with the standoff erupting in violence and looting two weeks ago.

For our standalone story on protests in France today, click here.

After a day of youth protests in Germany, senior police union representative Andreas Rosskopf said that there was no widespread property damage "so far."

"The Gen Z protests have turned out to be very peaceful," Rosskopf told the daily Rhenische Post.

While confrontations were reported after the marches ended in multiple cities, the people driving the clashes were "individuals acting independently, some of whom were masked."

Rosskopf, who represents Germany's federal police, said security forces acted very decisively and forcefully when such response was appropriate.

"Security forces remain absolutely ready to prevent any further clashes in the late evening of overnight," he said.

German security forces reported minor violent incidents in several cites in the wake of the Gen Z demonstrations.

In Hamburg, protesters at the city's Steintor square pelted the police with fireworks . Police used "immediate force" to clear the area, including using a water cannon.

Several police officers were injured during a similar incident in Frankfurt, according to a state interior minister.

Police also used a water cannon in Cologne, where the march was halted and turned into a stationary rally after some protesters covered their faces and used pyrotechnics.

A police officers sustained light injuries in nearby Bonn during a confrontation with a group of protesters.

In Berlin, the authorities noted a rally separate from the official event organized by the Gen Z movement. Police initially reported "isolated instances of throwing eggs and bottles" from a crowd of around 500 people. The authorities later also reported "illegal burning of pyrotechnics" and said the crowd has grown to around 3,000 participants.

Several police officers were injured in a clash with a group of protesters following the Gen Z demonstration in Frankfurt, authorities said.

"One officers could be injured more seriously, but this will need some more looking into," said Hesse Interior Minister Roman Poseck.

"We assume there were about 100 attackers motivated by extreme leftist ideology," the state minister said.

"They have staged a massive attack against the police by throwing bottles, stones and fireworks."

Police responded with water cannons and have the situation in hand, he said

Thousands of young people took part in protests in 34 German cities on Saturday.

German Gen Z protesters called out rising living expenses, remilitarization of Germany, and declining education.

Some of the protesters also called for Germany's current chancellor, center-right Friedrich Merz, to step down.

The protests were held under the slogan Gen Z regelt (Gen Z sorts it).

Police were out in force after many politicians warned that Germany will not tolerate the kind of violence seen in France in mid-October.

Police reported incidents in which pepper spray and water cannon were used to keep crowds under control, with protesters setting off fireworks and lighting fires.

Most of the demonstrations ended peacefully.

But tensions remained high in some German cities with reports of several police officers injured.

In Germany's second-biggest city, Hamburg, police estimated 6,700 people taking part in the demonstration.

They reported some groups of black-clad protesters, some of whom also wore face masks, pulling apart construction site barriers and throwing them on the street. Some of the barriers were later set on fire.

Police said they pushed the crowd back and used pepper spray to break them apart. The fire was eventually put out.

Following an initial estimate of several hundred people attending the rally in central Berlin, police said that some 5,000 people were now gathered at the Brandenburg Gate. The organizers, "Gen Z regelt" (Gen Z sorts it) gave a much higher number, saying 10,000 people were in attendance.

One of the speakers in Berlin, Kaja Schwab, decried false promises made by politicians.

The youth is being told that "we will do well if we work hard enough." In reality, the life is getting unaffordable and the young are "forced into military service," she said, in reference to Germany's renewed recruitment drive.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Thousands of young people have joined the demonstrations in over 30 German cities, with police reporting largely peaceful protests.

Hundreds also gathered in Hamburg, Erfurt, Magdeburg, Dresden, Leipzig,  Nuremberg, and elsehwere.

Retailers in several city centers had boarded up shop windows, particularly along luxury shopping streets, fearing unrest. Some shops were already closed for the Reformation Day public holiday.

No nationwide turnout figure was immediately available. More than 182,100 people had expressed interest in attending the events online.

Police in Cologne called off the planned "Gen Z regelt" procession after some participants covered their faces and used pyrotechnics.

"The demonstration will continue as a stationary rally," a police spokeswoman told the DPA news agency. Participants would remain on the Rhine riverbank, she said, appealing for restraint.

Attendance remained below the 15,000 people registered for the demonstration. Based on advance registrations, Cologne's protest was expected to be the largest in North Rhine-Westphalia.

Police repeatedly stopped a youth protest march in Stuttgart, citing participants covering their faces and leaving the agreed route.

Officers also reported smoke devices and firecrackers before the procession began. "Be loud, but remain peaceful," a police spokeswoman urged in a video.

In other German cities, police reported a largely peaceful start to demonstrations. Authorities estimated included 2,500 participants in Freiburg, more than 1,500 in Frankfurt, 1,200 in Mainz, 1,000 in Munich and 650 in Berlin.

No nationwide turnout figure was immediately available.

Politicians must involve young people in decision-making or risk the youth turning away from political institutions, education researcher Nina Kolleck warned.

Their exclusion "creates the impression that there is a policy for the old, but not for the young," the University of Potsdam professor told Germany's RBB Inforadio.

Kolleck pointed to decades of underinvestment in schools and the disproportionate impact of climate change on younger generations.

She warned that populist parties could exploit the resulting political vacuum if young people's frustrations continued to go unanswered.

#736. Viktor Gyökeres the difference as Arsenal claim nervy win against Slavia Prague

Another European away day, another victory for Arsenal: albeit only just. This time, Viktor Gyökeres stole the show as poor Slavia Prague matched the longest winless streak in European Cup and Champions League history despite a spirited late comeback. That unwanted record stands at 23, equalling the mark set by AEK Athens and FCSB – formerly known as Steaua Bucharest – while Arsenal are unbeaten in their 10 last away trips. But had it not been for a wonder save from David Raya, the Czech champions would have snatched a point after Wiktor Nowak pulled one back late on as Mikel Arteta’s usually watertight defence showed signs of fallibility under pressure.

In contrast to last week’s defeat against Fleetwood in the Carabao Cup, Arsenal had been cruising until the last 15 minutes after Noni Madueke fired them ahead early on, set up superbly by Gyökeres.

That was the Sweden striker’s third assist in his past five appearances, although Arteta will have been even more encouraged by the emphatic finish that appeared to put the game beyond Slavia’s reach just before the break.

But the Arsenal manager admitted his side had taken their eye off the ball by allowing their hosts back into the game with some uncharacteristic defensive lapses as Slavia racked up 18 shots to his side’s 12.

“At half-time, the message was clear: there is still a lot to do in this game,” said Arteta. “We were extremely far from our standards in everything that we have to do, in every basic, in every concept and in everything that we discussed to avoid the game that we played in the second half. That is a huge learning.”

Slavia’s solitary victory in this competition came in their first-ever match in 2007 and after losing 3-0 to Arsenal here exactly a year ago, they knew their chances of avoiding the unwanted milestone were extremely slim. Arteta’s side have developed a killer instinct on their travels in Europe – not since May 2025 in the second leg of their semi-final against Paris Saint-Germain have Arsenal lost an away game in 90 minutes.

After their exploits at Anfield on Sunday that took them three points clear at the top of the Premier League, Arteta heavily rotated his side again with six changes. It’s perhaps not surprising that Martín Zubimendi ran out of steam given the Spain World Cup winner made only his third start of a frustrating campaign.

For the third time in Arsenal’s past four matches, Gyökeres was entrusted with leading the line after finally getting off the mark with a scrappy strike against Fleetwood. He finished as top scorer last season with 21 goals but has clearly been struggling for form and confidence. Yet there was no doubting the quality of his assist for Madueke’s opening goal after just eight minutes.

Raya’s long ball should have been dealt with by the Slavia defence but they made the criminal error of ­allowing it to bounce. That was the cue for Gyökeres to come alive as he beat his marker to the ball, chested it down and played the perfect pass for the England forward to run on to and score. Arteta’s reaction on the touchline suggested he enjoyed it too.

Mikel Merino was Arsenal’s hero here last year with two goals and he could have extended their lead on three occasions before the half-hour mark. The lively Madueke created his best opportunity after cutting the ball back to Merino but he could not beat Nazar Domchak in Slavia’s goal.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

With Martin Ødegaard watching from the bench next to William Saliba on his return from a long-term back injury, Arsenal lacked some of their usual fluency in attack. But ­Slavia were still no match for them and their task became almost ­impossible seven minutes before the break. Gyökeres exchanged a smart one-two with Merino inside the area before curling a brilliant shot into the far corner.

To their credit, the hosts began the second half with much more aggression after introducing their record signing, Ange N’Guessan, from the bench. Ezri Konsa and Declan Rice both found themselves in the book as Arsenal were pinned back. David Jurasek let fly from long range and his effort was deflected just wide of Raya’s goal. From the resulting corner, Gabriel Magalhães somehow managed to clear two goalbound headers off the line in a matter of seconds. The Brazilian celebrated with a massive fist pump but his evening wasn’t over.

Mikulas Konecny should have done much better with another header before Raya managed to push Oskar Kubiak’s header on to the post despite being at full stretch in mid-air. Slavia eventually scored the goal all their endeavour deserved in the final minute of normal time when Nowak fired in at the far post. There were a few nervous moments in stoppage time as Konecny forced Raya into another save. Arteta breathed a sigh of relief at the full-time whistle as Slavia were condemned to their fate.

#735. An island in mourning: Tenerife processes death of De Miguel

Fans have been paying their respects to Tenerife's Jesus de Miguel following his death on Tuesday

As you arrive on the holiday island of Tenerife, there is a profound sense of grief, pain and disbelief at the death of footballer Jesus de Miguel.

The Canary island is in mourning for the Tenerife striker, who died from injuries sustained in a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a match on Monday.

The 30-year-old had quickly established himself as a club favourite, scoring 11 goals in his first season as Tenerife were promoted to the second tier of Spanish football.

But now the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez Stadium has become a shrine to the player, with hundreds of people gathering throughout the past few days to lay flowers, light candles and pay their respects.

Bouquets, rosettes sent by clubs from across Spain, prayer cards, photographs, children's drawings and scarves have been laid around the grounds outside gate nine.

It is a deeply moving scene. Fans and residents stand in silence, taking in the tributes.

Many are visibly tearful as the scale of the loss begins to sink in at the very place the incident happened.

'Most difficult days of my life' for keeper Owono

Among those paying their respects were Lisa and Lee, visiting Tenerife from Stoke-on-Trent.

They had arrived on holiday at the weekend and decided to attend Monday's match, hoping to experience Spanish football for the first time.

"We never expected something like this to happen," they told BBC Sport.

"We knew it was serious when the players surrounded him [De Miguel], but to see players crying and actually praying on the pitch was very emotional.

"When we found out the news the next day, it just really hit us."

The couple described the atmosphere inside the stadium as sombre and almost completely silent as spectators waited to understand what was happening.

"You always expect somebody to pull through," Lee said. "And then seeing the news the next day, it was just unbelievable."

They returned to the stadium on Wednesday to lay a Port Vale shirt among the tributes, wanting to show their support for the Tenerife community.

"Football has no colours," Lisa said. "If it was one of our players, we'd be heartbroken. They're part of your family."

For Carlos, a player with Tenerife's disability side Tenerife Foundation, the loss is particularly personal.

"Honestly, there are no words to describe him. He was incredible," Carlos said as he lay a flag on the ground.

He described De Miguel as a figure who had helped shape the club's recent history.

"He practically gave his heart and soul for the shirt. He's already a legend at the club because, after all, we were in a very difficult position a few years ago and he helped pull us out of it.

"Without him, I don't think we would be where we are today."

Carlos was at Monday's match and said he was left in shock by what unfolded.

"When I left the stadium I was trembling and I continued to feel that way for hours.

"Right now, we're incredibly hurt and very sad. I also want to send my support to his family, who I can only imagine must be absolutely devastated."

English fans in Tenerife pay tribute to De Miguel

The sense of loss has extended far beyond the stadium.

Poli Suarez, the Canary Islands' minister for education and sport, said Tenerife was in "complete mourning".

"Canarian sport has been left devastated," Suarez told BBC Sport. "The club is broken. Absolutely heartbroken."

Suarez also stressed that the thoughts of everyone were with De Miguel's wife, daughter and wider family.

"They are the ones suffering most directly from this loss, just as the Tenerife supporters are suffering," he said.

The government has pledged its support to the club, players and supporters, with Suarez describing De Miguel as a footballer who had become part of the Canary Islands' sporting history.

"The loss of Jesus de Miguel is now part of our history," Suarez said.

"Not only because of the circumstances of his death, but also because of the affection he always showed towards our island and towards his club."

A further tribute is planned for Saturday at 18:00 GMT, with supporters encouraged to come together to honour his memory.

"It will be an opportunity to show our affection and emotion, and to demonstrate our solidarity with the family," Suarez said.

"We want to show all our affection for Jesus de Miguel."

"Happy 18th birthday!" Jon wrote on Instagram in 2022. "Today is your birthday we gonna say it loud. I love you. Love, Dad."

"Our big celebration of #15 is finally winding down here! We celebrated ALL DAY LONG, beginning with a present at 6:30 am before school! I'm so very thankful for my ‘babies'.... somehow they are 15 already?!" Kate wrote on the special milestone in 2019. "I'm amazed by them each day! I'm so proud of the positive qualities I've seen developing as they edge closer to adulthood."

"This was yesterday! Feels like school never ended...and they're already back! #SeniorYear #EighthGrade #ProudMom," Kate wrote on Instagram in 2018.

"Happy 15th Birthday Hannah, Collin, Alexis, Aaden, Joel and Leah!!!! Wow I can't believe you are 15!!! Time is flying by!!!" Jon Gosselin shared on Instagram when posing with Hannah and Collin Gosselin. "I love you all very much. I wish you the best day ever and I hope you enjoy your birthday celebrations today and this weekend!!! Love always, Dad."

"My beautiful 'little girls' .... they keep reminding me how many days until they turn 14. Today it was '12 days til we turn 14, Mom.' HOW'S THAT EVEN POSSIBLE?!" Kate shared with her followers in 2018. "I told Leah that she's too small to turn 14. She said 'Yeah, true. Are you sure I'm not turning 11 or 12?' I'm positive. I gave birth to you. They'll always be my babies....I love them so very much!"

"I can't believe they're 13!" Kate Gosselin wrote on Instagram when celebrating a major birthday for her sextuplets.

Rewind to 2014 when Kate and her children found themselves visiting Alaska.

Kate also treated her twin daughters Cara Gosselin and Mady Gosselin to a trip to New York City in 2014, where they stopped by the Manhattan Hotel.

"A precious Christmas memory. My 6 were 6. Christmas Eve 2010 and they're SO excited for Christmas!" Kate Gosselin wrote on Instagram with a throwback photo. "Look at those adorable smiles! #TheyAreMyHeart #My8ReasonsToKeepOnKeepingOn #NoMatterWhat #TrueLoveX8."

Back in October 2007, Jon and Kate Gosselin gathered their eight kids together for a trip to New York City. First stop? A visit to NBC's Today show.

#732. Muriqi caps Fenerbahce comeback to make Liverpool pay for defensive lapses

Andoni Iraola arrived in Istanbul seeking improvement from Liverpool’s attack but departed with sudden cause for concern at the opposite end of the pitch. Fenerbahce ignited Dirk Kuyt’s interim spell with a tumultuous victory after Liverpool detonated their 100% Champions League record with several defensive lapses.

Liverpool’s second successive defeat left Iraola exasperated for entirely different reasons to Sunday’s loss to Arsenal. Blame was found only in the mirror this time around. It was so careless and so unnecessary.

The visitors led twice, through Trey Nyoni’s first senior goal and a header from substitute Alexander Isak, but Fenerbahce twice hit back quickly and snatched victory when Vedat Muriqi emerged as the strongest player from a pack of red shirts. Fenerbahce’s first goal came from a free-kick, their second from a corner and their third from a long throw-in.

“Cheap goals, messy goals,” as the Liverpool head coach put it. “We knew set pieces were one of the strengths of Fenerbahce. We have been dealing with them well, both this season and today, it has been something we have been working on since pre-season, but it cost us today. The last goal was maybe because they are strong and tall but the other two we have to control better.”

Ronald Araújo resting on the bench offers one explanation for Liverpool’s weak defensive display but does not cover every fault. The visitors enjoyed large spells of control and, despite an anonymous display from Bradley Barcola as the central striker, should never have given hope to an ageing, average Fenerbahce side packed with familiar names from the Premier League.

As expected, Turkish supporters tested the eardrums with incessant whistling whenever Liverpool took possession. They were a test for structural engineers too with their constant bouncing in the upper tier of the home end. Liverpool sought to dilute the atmosphere by controlling possession. Rio Ngumoha was prominent and N’Golo Kanté should have been booked for halting one promising run by leaping on the teenager’s back. Referee Clément Turpin was in a lenient mood with both sides.

Fenerbahce had struggled to hold up play in the Liverpool half or create a chance of note when Archie Brown exposed the visiting defence with a superb ball from left-back. The pass sailed over the struggling Kostas Tsimikas and was controlled well by Mason Greenwood, before he was pushed over by the Liverpool defender. Neither Turpin nor the video assistant referee deemed it a penalty kick.

The decibel levels cranked up and went even higher when Liverpool took the lead moments later. Ngumoha was heavily involved with a darting run and shot that was charged down into the path of Dominik Szoboszlai. Brown, under pressure from Virgil van Dijk, headed the midfielder’s cross clear but only as far as Nyoni. The young midfielder swept a low volley beyond Ederson with the aid of a slight deflection off Kojo Peprah Oppong. It was a memorable milestone in the continued rise of Nyoni; the first goal of his career at the highest level.

It was also the cue for Fenerbahce to rouse themselves. The hosts almost levelled straight from the restart when Brown’s low centre was turned against Alisson’s crossbar by Irfan Can Kahveci, who may have been ruled offside. They did not have to wait long for the equaliser. After Szoboszlai was penalised for a foul on Kanté, Greenwood’s resulting free-kick took a huge deflection off Jérémy Jacquet’s stomach and sailed past the wrongfooted Alisson. The Liverpool keeper did not hide his anger at Jacquet turning away from the free-kick and leaving a costly hole in the wall.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

The second half mirrored the first with Liverpool in control until scoring and provoking a reaction from the Turkish side. Substitutes Cody Gakpo and Isak had only been on the pitch three minutes when they combined to restore the visitors’ advantage, the Swedish striker heading past Ederson from Gakpo’s left-wing cross.

But Fenerbahce again levelled swiftly when Kanté swept in a cross following a corner and Gakpo, attempting to head clear, glanced the ball away from Alisson’s grasp to give Brown a simple tap-in at the back post. “In the stadium it was almost impossible to communicate,” Iraola admitted. “It was difficult for me to give instructions and the communication must have been difficult between Cody and Ali.”

Worse was to come for Liverpool when Birmingham-born Brown looped a cross into the heart of Liverpool’s box. Muriqi, a second-half replacement for Romelu Lukaku, managed to hold off three Liverpool players – Jacquet, Alexis Mac Allister and Nyoni – and plant a header into the bottom corner. Iraola added: “It’s so frustrating because this is a difficult place to play and we were winning twice. We need to look at how we conceded the goals.”

#731. Pregnant Savannah Chrisley Bares Her Baby Bump on Chick-fil-A Run

Savannah Chrisley, who announced her pregnancy with husband Jason Galanis last week, grabbed lunch at Chick-fil-A in an outfit that gave a peek at her baby bump.

Savannah Chrisley’s baby knows best—he wants fried chicken.

After all, the pregnant Chrisley Knows Best alum was spotted putting her baby bump on display during a recent trip to Chick-fil-A.

During the Nov. 3 outing in Nashville, Chrisley sported a pair of gray sweatpants and a body-hugging, long-sleeved black T-shirt that rode up a bit, giving a peek at her stomach.

The 29-year-old also donned the massive engagement ring she received from husband Jason Galanis, 56, whom she privately married in the Cayman Islands over the summer.

Days before her jaunt to the popular southern chicken joint, Chrisley showed off her growing baby bump at the annual Mar-a-Lago Halloween party, which she attended in a special Tree of Life costume that featured a cutout around her stomach.

While Chrisley continues to embrace her changing body, she has also found herself defending her pregnancy with Galanis, who served part of his federal prison sentence alongside her dad Todd Chrisley.

"You are not a headline," the Unlocked podcast host wrote on her Instagram Stories Oct. 27, addressing her unborn baby. "You are not a controversy. You are not defined by anyone's past, anyone's mistakes, or anyone's opinions. You are innocent, deeply loved, and the greatest blessing God could have ever entrusted your daddy and I with."

She added, "No amount of noise in this world will ever overshadow the joy of being your mama. You are my answered prayer. And I will never apologize for celebrating you."

Meanwhile, in the aftermath of revealing her pregnancy, engagement and marriage within the span of a week, Chrisley has also acknowledged the “huge” age gap in her relationship.

"That's probably part of the reason why I kept a lot of it quiet, because I know how brutal the public can be," she said on the Oct. 27 episode of Unlocked. “But I genuinely do not care."

As Chrisley sees it, "I have always said, 'I would rather 20 phenomenal, unbelievable years with someone than 50 just meh years.’ The amount of love and respect that we have—we have so many dreams, and we dream together, we work together."

For a deeper dive into the Chrisley family tree, keep reading…

Todd Chrisley is the patriarch of the Chrisley family.He was born in Georgia in April 1969 and raised in South Carolina. He and first wife Teresa Terry welcomed daughter Lindsie Chrisley in 1989 and son Kyle Chrisley in 1991 before splitting a few years later. After their breakup, Todd wed Julie Chrisley (born in South Carolina in January 1973) in 1996.Together, they added to their family with the births of kids Chase Chrisley, Savannah Chrisley and Grayson Chrisley and the adoption of Kyle's daughter Chloe Chrisley. They also went through challenges, including Julie's 2012 breast cancer battle (she's now cancer-free).As Todd said on the premiere of Chrisley Knows Best—a show that followed the family's ups and downs as well as their rich lifestyle in Atlanta and later Nashville—he made "95 percent" of their money through his real estate business before entering reality TV. As for Julie, she was working at a bank when she started dating Todd. Chrisley Knows Best ran from 2014 to 2023 and led to spin-offs like Growing Up Chrisley and What's Cooking With Julie? as well as other media ventures like the family members' podcasts.In 2022, Todd and Julie were convicted of fraud and tax crimes, and they were originally sentenced to 12 and seven years in prison, respectively (with him being held in Florida and her being behind bars in Kentucky). The couple pleaded not guilty.In May 2025, President Donald Trump pardoned Todd and Julie and they were released from prison.

Born in September 1989, Lindsie is Todd's eldest daughter from his marriage to Teresa.She attended Georgia State University, where she met now-ex husband Will Campbell. They wed in 2012, and she graduated and gave birth to their son Jackson that December. Two years later, Chrisley Knows Best premiered.Lindsie appeared on the series for five seasons, where viewers saw how Todd and Will didn't get along. She and Will filed for divorce in 2016, and she left the show in 2017.In the years following, there was public fallout between her and her family. It wasn't until 2022 that Lindsie, Todd, Julie and Savannah reunited publicly on crossover episodes of their podcasts.However, their reunion was short-lived. In a 2025 episode of her podcast The Southern Tea, Lindsie said she hasn't seen her dad "in quite some time." The following month, she confirmed she's also estranged from her siblings."We can live in the same space doing the same things and not necessarily agree or align and it’s no hate, it’s no ill will," Lindsie said on Catelynn Lowell and Tyler Baltierra’s podcast, Cate & Ty Break It Down in 2025. "We just don’t serve each other in each other’s lives."In May 2026, Lindsie was arrested on suspicion of DUI, attempting to elude police, improper passing and reckless driving and speeding."I got pulled over speeding past a car on a two lane road," she told TMZ, "because they almost hit an animal and I was trying to miss hitting them and whatever the animal was."

Kyle, born in August 1991, is Todd’s eldest son from his former marriage to Teresa. In November 2012, he became father to daughter Chloe, whose mother is his ex Angela Johnson. But in 2016, Todd and Julie adopted Chloe.While Kyle appeared on only the first season of Chrisley Knows Best (aside from a brief cameo in 2021), his past arrests and rocky relationship with his family (which involved them being estranged and reuniting at various points in time) continued to make headlines. He’s also spoken candidly about his mental health journey and battle with addiction, sharing in a 2019 Facebook post that he's sober.In 2021, Kyle wed Ashley Nelson and became a father to her kids Haiden and Mackenzie.As for where Kyle stands with Todd and Julie, he expressed his hope to reconnect with them after their return from prison."I know they can't wait to get home and just be with family," he told E! News in May 2025, "and I'm going to remain hopeful that another reconciliation is possible."

Chase is the first child Todd welcomed with wife Julie, arriving in June 1996.In addition to appearing on Chrisley Knows Best with his parents and siblings, the entrepreneur co-starred on Growing Up Chrisley with his sister Savannah from 2019 to 2022. Chase was previously engaged to Emmy Medders. But after breaking up and getting back together, they officially parted ways in 2023.After Chase's parents entered prison, he spoke about how he and his siblings came together."We've definitely gotten a lot closer," he told Extra in 2023. "When you get hit with something like this, I feel like a lot of people either separate and go their own ways or they cling together, which is how we were raised. We've clung together and we're still fighting."Chase had his own run-in with the law in January 2025, when he was arrested in Atlanta on a simple battery charge for allegedly becoming "really drunk" and slapping a bar manager after being asked to leave, according to police records obtained by E! News. His lawyers told People that "this incident has been entirely blown out of proportion.""He did not assault anyone," they added. "Chase was trying to close out his tab and leave. We will be independently investigating the situation."

Todd and Julie welcomed daughter Savannah in August 1997.Early in her career, she competed in the pageant world—winning Miss Tennessee Teen USA in 2016 and vying for the Miss Teen USA crown later that year. However, her time in the limelight didn't end there as she went on to appear on several reality and competition shows, including Chrisley Knows Best, Growing Up Chrisley, The Masked Singer and Special Forces: World's Toughest Test. Savannah is also a real estate agent in Tennessee, the founder of Good Girl RX and host of the podcast Unlocked.In her personal life, Savannah got engaged to hockey player Nic Kerdiles in 2019. However, they broke up the following year, and he died after a motorcycle crash in 2023. She later dated Robert Shiver; however, she confirmed their split in April 2025 after about two years together. Savannah obtained custody of her brother Grayson and sister Chloe while Julie and Todd were in prison and advocated for her parents' release.After Trump pardoned Julie and Todd and they were released from prison, Savannah posted footage from their return home, including one that read "Reunited and it feels so good."In October 2026, Savannah announced she's engaged—with her fiancé revealed as Jason Galanis, who served time in the same prison as Todd before receiving his own presidential pardon in 2025—and that they're expecting a baby.

Grayson is Todd and Julie's youngest son.Born in May 2006, Grayson entered the spotlight when Chrisley Knows Best premiered eight years later. He's now a student at the University of Alabama—and yes, he gets recognized on campus."It's been insane," he said on a February 2025 episode of Savannah's podcast Unlocked. "It's more than it's ever happened here."After Julie and Todd went to prison, Savannah gained custody of Grayson and Chloe."I’m not their mom. I’m not their dad. I’m their sister and I get to love and guide them through life," the podcaster wrote on Instagram in July 2023. "Being a bonus parent is TOUGH…no one could ever add up to their parents. But these kiddos have shown me so much love, patience, grace, understanding, and appreciation! Helping to raise these two kiddos is the hardest but most rewarding job I will ever have."And Savannah's bond with Grayson grew even stronger."Many people look at our situation and think, 'She saved him,'" she wrote on Instagram for his 18th birthday in May 2024, "but little do they know… YOU saved ME."

Todd and Julie started out as Chloe's grandparents after his son Kyle fathered the child with ex Angela Johnson in November 2012. However, they adopted her four years later.“My heart!” Julie wrote on Instagram in February 2018. “This child brings so much happiness to our family. What did we do without you?”Fans watched Todd and Julie raise Chloe—or CoCo as her family calls her—on Chrisley Knows Best. But after the couple entered prison, Savannah took over as her guardian.“Watching her grow has been the biggest blessing of my life… she has QUITE the personality!” Savannah wrote on Instagram for Chloe’s 11th birthday in November 2023. "I wish I had her humor. I wish I had her carefree spirit. I wish I had her heart. She is everything that I hope to be one day! There is not a day goes by to where she doesn’t reach me something new. Because of her… we are all better people! I love you sweet girl! KEEP SHINING! NEVER GIVE UP! And ALWAYS KNOW… I AM HERE!”After it was announced that Trump was pardoning Todd and Julie, Savannah shared Chloe’s reaction. "Chloe I think is still in shock, and she doesn't want to get her hopes up because she feels like something bad's going to happen," she said on a May 2025 episode of News Nation. "But I'm excited to be going to get my dad and bringing him home to her."

Faye Chrisley—a.k.a. "Nanny"—is Todd's mom."I am blessed beyond measure that God chose you to be my mother," he wrote on Instagram for Mother's Day in 2021. "I love you more than you will ever know and you fill my heart with love, hope, faith and confidence."Born in September 1944, Nanny grew up in South Carolina. She married army veteran Gene Chrisley, and they welcomed sons Todd, Randy Chrisley and Derrick Chrisley, the latter of whom died when he was a baby. Gene also passed away in 2012.While on Chrisley Knows Best, Nanny captured fans' hearts with her humor, fun times with sister Frances (who died in 2022), dating adventures and advice. And whether she was hitting the casino, raising a glass of wine or spending time with family, she proved to viewers she knows how to have a good time.However, Nanny has gone through hard times too. In addition to Todd and Julie's convictions, Nanny was diagnosed with bladder cancer in 2021. But two years later, she shared she had overcome her health battle."I’m in remission, thank God," Nanny said on a 2023 episode of Lindsie's podcast The Southern Tea, per People. "I’ve been out moving around, doing the best I can."Doing the best she can has been Nanny's approach to life in general."The world don’t always give you a good deck of cards to play with, so you play with them the best you can," she said on Savannah's podcast Unlocked in 2023. "You get up, brush yourself off and keep going."

#728. Pregnant SLOMW Star Jen Affleck Files for Divorce from Zac Affleck

The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives' Jen Affleck, who is pregnant with her and Zac Affleck's fourth baby, has filed for divorce after seven years of marriage.

Jen Affleck's marriage with Zac Affleck couldn't survive MomTok.

The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star—mom to kids Nora, 4, Luca, 3, and Penelope, 15 months, with a fourth baby on the way—filed for divorce from Zac on Nov. 3 after eight years together and seven years of marriage, according to court documents obtained by TMZ.

E! News has reached out to Jen's rep for comment but hasn't heard back.

In recent years, Jen—who announced her pregnancy in June—and Zac's marriage troubles have been highly documented on Mormon Wivesand spinoff series The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County, which saw the duo move to Southern California as they prepared to welcome another child.

Of course, with so many life changes comes plenty of relationship stressors, as Jen recently revealed.

"It’s been a lot the past couple of months, I’ll be honest," Jen confessed to People in August. "But I do feel like I’m seeing the light at the end of the tunnel and just trying to count my blessings every single day."

While Jen wasn't yet ready to say the "D" word at the time, she did admit, "There’s a lot that we’ve been navigating behind closed doors."

For starters, the 27-year-old struggled with prenatal depression during a rough first trimester.

"I could not be there for my kids, and so Zac really had to show up," she told the outlet, adding that though "he didn’t really have a choice," she also "wouldn’t have survived the first trimester" without the 29-year-old, whom she met in 2018 and wed one year later.

Not only that, but navigating life's ups and downs in the public eye comes with an added level of scrutiny.

While breakup rumors are nothing new for the exes, Jen previously shot down speculation their sometimes-contentious bickering on SLOMW was an indication they were headed for a divorce.

"It can be tiring and draining, just because it gets old having to hear the same things," Jen exclusively told E! in November 2025. "For me, I’m like, 'People will always talk and people will always have their opinions,' and I think it is frustrating for him when people don’t see what’s happening behind closed doors and how much work and effort he’s putting in."

Ultimately, Jen—who has shared her past struggles with mental health issues—focused on "tuning out the noise of the world" when she felt overwhelmed.

"It’s hard to have to constantly open your phone and see negative comments and it’s hard not to take that in," the social media star explained. "Even if you say you don’t take it in, subconsciously we all care to a certain point. For me, I always have to remind myself, I post, I share my story, and then I take a step back. As long as I’m focusing on being the best version of myself, that’s all that matters."

While fans wait for more updates on Jen and Zac's split, keep reading to check in on where the rest of the Hulu hit's relationships stand.

Taylor Frankie Paul & Dakota Mortensen: Broken Up

While Taylor Frankie Paul's romance with Dakota Mortensen—they welcomed son Ever in 2024—bloomed on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, they called it quits due to Dakota's infidelity.

"Right after Ever was born, Dakota and I were living together and in bliss with our new baby, and I was even considering engagement," Taylor—who began dating the real estate agent in July 2022—revealed during the season two premiere of the Hulu series. "And then I learned that he was lying this entire time."

Taylor was told by a woman named Jenna that she and Dakota had been intimate and he had "spent the night more than once." (He has denied the claims, writing in a September 2024 TikTok that he "never cheated.")

On the series, Taylor said that Dakota accused Jenna of instigating their affair.

"No, it was him," she emphasized in the confessional. "He said he had just kissed her on the couch. No, he went on the couch, they hooked up on the couch, and then they went to the room and they hooked up."

Since ending her romance with the Basin Tiling founder, the mom of three (she shares two kids with ex-husband Tate Paul) was set to find love once again on season 22 of The Bachelorette, but things got a bit thorny when news broke in March 2026 of an alleged confrontation between the exes weeks earlier.

A spokesperson for the Draper City Police Department confirmed to People that there was an open "domestic assault investigation," telling the outlet "allegations have been made in both directions.”

Days later, a video of a previous 2023 physical altercation between Taylor and Dakota surfaced online, prompting ABC to cancel the MomToker's season of the dating franchise.

As for Dakota, he has kicked off a romance with show guest star Shinia Powell, though he previously apologized to Taylor for hooking up with her during a season four episode.

Whitney Leavitt & Connor Leavitt: Married

Whitney Leavitt found the perfect dance partner in Connor Leavitt, whom she wed in 2016. But it wasn't always smooth sailing for the couple—who share kids Sedona, Liam and Billy—as they navigated life in the spotlight.

For instance, the Dancing With the Stars alum, who announced during her Broadway run in May 2026 that she'd be leaving Mormon Wives, had to shut down rumors about her husband's sexuality.

"Do I need to put out a sex tape, or something? Like, trust me," she said on the Off the Vine podcast in October 2024. "We're good. Everything's fine."

"I think it's because when we were going through our personal stuff—and I know you haven't seen it—but he struggled through a porn addiction," she explained. "There's a scene where one of my friends says something along the lines of how they could see how he was confused sexually."

Through the ups and downs, the reality star emphasized that she and Connor—who were 23 and 22, respectively, when they got married—are stronger than ever. In fact, they even renewed their vows in February 2026 for their 10th wedding anniversary.

"We got married really young," Conner told Brides after their ceremony. "It felt like our wedding day, as much as it was for us, it really felt like it was for our families. So we really want to do something to make it ours, and this felt like a really fun way to do it."

While Jen Affleck and Zac Affleck—no relation to Ben Affleck, despite jokes to the contrary—have been married since 2019, the couple has been at the center of breakup rumors since season one.

In fact, their fight after Jen attended a Chippendales striptease show in Las Vegas became a focal point of the first season. The couple—who share kids Nora, Penelope and Lucas—made up, however, and the Dancing With the Stars contestant later defended their relationship.

"It can be tiring and draining, just because it gets old having to hear the same things," Jen told E! News of the speculations in November 2025. "For me, I'm like, 'People will always talk and people will always have their opinions.' I think it is frustrating for him when people don't see what's happening behind closed doors and how much work and effort he's putting in."

So, she and Zac are focusing on what really matters: "We're working on just tuning out the noise of the world—I think it still is hard for him." Jen announced in June 2026 that she'd be adding to their dance troupe with baby No. 4.

Jessi Draper & Jordan Ngatikaura: Divorcing

Bumps in Jessi Draper and Jordan Ngatikaura's five-year marriage emerged after the hairstylist admitted to having an emotional affair with Vanderpump Villa's Marciano Brunette, though initially it appeared they were working towards smoother roads.

"We are back together," Jessi—who shares kids Jagger and Jovi with Jordan—told E! News in November 2025. "We're trying to work on it. Relationships are not perfect. I think a situation like ours—it's going to take time. It's not going to something that's just amazing overnight."

Sadly, the reconciliation appeared to be short-lived, with Jordan also dad to daughter Peyton from a previous relationship, filing for divorce in March 2026 after five years of marriage.

However, days later, Jessi said she was “blindsided” by his filing and accused him of rushing to submit the paperwork because “he wanted the headline first.”

Admitting that her “heart sunk” seeing the news, she explained, “because we agreed to tell our children together before filing and we haven’t done that.” (E! reached out to attorneys for Jordan for comment but haven’t heard back.)

Though Jessi told E! News that she was "just casually dating and living life," when she brought Marciano as her date to the 2026 American Music Awards in May 2026, he revealed a tattoo dedicated to her that August.

Mayci didn't expect to find love with Jacob Neeley. In fact, after the unexpected death of her boyfriend Arik Mack in 2015, when she was just 14 weeks pregnant with their son Hudson, she was prepared to be a single mom.

But it all changed when she met Jacob in 2016 at age 21, whom she would marry two years later.

"After everything I'd been through, I was very guarded, but Jacob was kind and we got on really well," Mayci said in her memoir Told You So. "For a long time, we remained just friends and because we weren't really dating, I was OK with him meeting my son."

"Jacob was amazing with him, which made him appear even more attractive," she continued. "I was terrified of getting hurt again but, after four months, I couldn't deny my feelings any longer. He was kind and funny and made me feel safe."

Mayci and Jacob went on to welcome daughters Harlow in 2021 and Charli in 2025.

Demi Engemann and her husband Bret Engemann tied the knot in 2021, one year after she and Blake Corbin divorced. As the couple's relationship played out on the reality show, their sexual explorations became a major plot point after Whitney gifted Demi a box of Fruity Pebbles.

The truth behind the joke gift wasn't revealed until Jessi shared on Instagram in November 2025 that "grandpa Bret likes to drink her piss like it's dirty soda and he gulps it down like water."

But Demi and Bret aren't crying over spilled secrets—or pee. In fact, she told Entertainment Tonight that December that she and Bret "have nothing else left to do other than own it and have fun with it."

Although their sex life raised eyebrows, the couple has been embracing life with their blended family. While Demi shares daughter Maude with her ex, Bret is dad to his and The Real Housewives of Salt Lake City alum Angie Harrington's sons Rome and Cole.

"I've never seen a dad so involved or love their kids harder, the most devoted step-dad to Maude, and future father to our own children one day," Demi wrote on Instagram in June 2024. "Your ability to remain consistently loyal to your role as father/step-father while navigating all that life throws your way, will never cease to amaze me!"

Mikayla Matthews and Jace Terry have been through it all together. While The reality star first met Jace in 2015 when she was 15 and they welcomed their first son Beckham two years later. Since then, the couple—who tied the knot in 2018—welcomed kids Haven, Tommie and Lottie.

While Mikayla and Jace have been loving life with their four kids, Mikayla admitted that she hopes to grow their family even further.

"When people ask me how many kids I want, I'm like, 'I've always wanted three or four, but I could see myself having six,'" she told People in February 2025. "I'm excited to hopefully move into a new house. I want a big lot for my herd of kids."

However, Mikayla confirmed in the ninth episode of the show's fourth season that she and Jace were taking time apart amid ongoing intimacy struggles.

As Mikayla began unpacking her trauma surrounding years of sexual abuse as a teen, as well as her chronic illness—which causes flare-ups due to heightened stress—their marriage had been deeply affected.

"I think it's hard anytime you bring up the stuff with the sex or the intimacy," she admitted to Jace. "I feel like it's hard on me 'cause I feel like, again, my nervous system's already in fight or flight and I'm already maxed out. My bucket is full."

After Layla Taylor and Clayton Wessel—who are parents to sons Oliver and Maxwell—divorced in 2023, the reality star teased her new romance with Mason McWhorter in July 2025.

Their relationship was a bit complicated on paper. Hang with us: Mason's brother is Chase McWhorter, the ex-husband of Layla's costar Miranda McWhorter. But the pair had been willing to put their romance to the test.

"Right now, I'm kind of scared of marriage but I just want to get to know somebody very well before I even consider that," Layla told Us in November 2025. "I'm just happy and content where me and Mason are. And if somehow that ever were to come up, then we would see."

Unfortunately, the mom of two confirmed that she and Mason had split in February 2026.

"I think we were just on two different paths right now, and he felt in order for him to grow, he had to be on his own," Layla shared. "I respect his decision, and I truly hope that he gets what he wants in life."

As for Layla, who came out as bisexual in June 2026, she soft-launched her romance with a mystery woman a month later in an Instagram video. She later seemed to confirm her relationship with Colorado-based content creator Kelsie Chesser.

Miranda McWhorter & Chase McWhorter: Divorced

Although Miranda is a newer addition to The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, joining in season two, she played a major role in the infamous MomTok "soft swinging scandal." Despite the situation with Taylor, Miranda revealed that drama wasn't the reason for her 2024 divorce from Chase.

"The reasons why we decided to split were things that were issues far before that,” she explained on the Weekly Trash podcast in August 2024. "That might not have helped, for sure, but it definitely did not play a part in the decision process."

Nonetheless, she and Chase have been committed to parenting their kids Brooks and Cohen.

"With co-parenting, you're always having to work on it," she reflected. “The thing is that if we got along perfectly all the time and it was just rainbows and butterflies, we probably wouldn't have gotten divorced."

"The thing with him and I," she continued, "we've always had a pretty good foundation of a friendship prior to even having a romantic relationship. I feel like that's something that set us up for some level of success when it comes to co-parenting."

#726. Another 'miracle' in Istanbul - but this one hurt Liverpool

Liverpool suffer first Champions League loss to Fenerbahce

When it comes to comebacks, Liverpool and Istanbul have plenty of history - but this time Andoni Iraola's side made the wrong kind.

Having hit the front for a second time against Fenerbahce, when Alexander Isak nodded in after 69 minutes, Liverpool were seemingly on their way to a thoroughly impressive away win.

But Iraola's players then capitulated amid a febrile atmosphere, as spirited hosts led by interim boss Dirk Kuyt - a Liverpool hero of years gone by - pulled off a shock Champions League comeback victory.

By losing 3-2 at the Sukru Saracoglu stadium, Iraola's visitors created that unwanted slice of history: this was the latest Liverpool have ever gone ahead in a major European game and then been beaten.

Iraola described the goals they conceded as "cheap" and "messy".

After Liverpool let three points slip from their grasp, Kuyt spoke of how he had encouraged Fenerbahce's players to embrace the never-say-die mindset that allowed the Reds to achieve so many great feats in Europe in the past.

He joined Liverpool in 2006, a year after the team's famous 'Miracle of Istanbul' comeback in the Champions League final, and spent six years as a first-team fixture.

"We told each other to stick together and be united. That's something I learned from Liverpool, who we played against," Kuyt said. "We made a miracle tonight - not many expected us to win."

He and Fenerbahce will remember this one for a long time. Liverpool will want to quickly forget it.

After winning five games in a row, Iraola's side have gone on to lose twice in four days. Arsenal on Sunday, and now this.

On the flight back from Istanbul, there will be plenty of disappointment at the way in which Liverpool failed to see this game out.

"It's frustration because it's a difficult place to come and play," said Iraola. "We were, during most part of the game, thinking we can win this one. But obviously it hasn't happened."

All three of Fenerbahce's goals came from set-pieces.

Former Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood benefited from a slice of luck when his free-kick deflected in off Jeremy Jacquet in the first half for Fenerbahce's first equaliser, and Liverpool only had themselves to blame when Cody Gakpo's header took the ball past Alisson and gave Birmingham-born Archie Brown a tap in to make it 2-2.

Six minutes later, Liverpool made a mess of Brown's looping ball in the box and Vedat Muriqi beat three players in red and headed past Alisson.

"They are cheap goals. They are messy goals," said Iraola.

"It's a free-kick. It's quite far also and it's through the wall.

"Mistakes can cost you. For the last goal, it's a long throw and the first phase is controlled but after a very long ball, Muriqi wins it.

"The second goal, Cody is the one touching the ball just in front of Ali [Alisson].

"In the stadium it was almost impossible to communicate because it was so noisy. It was even difficult for me to give any kind of instruction. I suppose the communication between Ali and Cody was difficult."

Liverpool lost 3-2 having twice been ahead against Fenerbahce

Kuyt's Fenerbahce fight back to beat Liverpool

After showing signs of genuine progress in recent weeks, Liverpool let potential victory slip away here in a concerning manner.

Trey Nyoni's first goal for the club had given them an early lead, but the teenager's deflected strike was cancelled out by Greenwood's reply in kind four minutes later.

The real drama came from the 69th minute to the 79th, with Liverpool inching ahead again, close to a fourth win in four in the competition, but unable to see the job through.

"It feels like a step back from what we saw against Arsenal because everyone thought, OK, we are seeing huge improvements from Liverpool," said ex-Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock, who was watching the game for Match of the Day.

"It was a much-changed team. However, the simple mistakes that they made from set-pieces or simple balls into the box are not good enough.

"The frustrating part for Liverpool fans is that we all know what the problems are. So, where is the solution? That's what Iraola is trying to do at the moment, but it's just a question of how long it takes.

"The biggest issue is that this keeps on happening, with Liverpool looking like they can concede at any moment and being so open on the counter-attack. There is a repetitive theme of the goals they are conceding and it undoes all the good work they do when they go forward.

"When you go ahead, twice, away from home at Fenerbahce in the Champions League then, if that is Arsenal they win that game - they see it out against a team like Fenerbahce.

"Liverpool don't have the ability to do that at the moment, and that is what is really frustrating."

Dirk Kuyt was a passionate presence on the touchline for Fenerbahce

On the eve of this game in the Kadikoy neighbourhood of Istanbul, Kuyt spoke passionately about how Fenerbahce had the opportunity to show Europe their true colours.

He will step aside now, with former Newcastle player Emre Belozoglu taking over as head coach officially from Thursday.

Thanks to this night, Europe now knows all about Fenerbahce.

They have had a torrid season so far, though, having lost four of their 10 league games, but Kuyt's men delivered a performance that will live long in the memory for anyone associated with the Turkish side.

"We showed Europe how big Fenerbahce is. This is what the spirit of this side is," said Kuyt.

"I think it's very special that for the first time since 18 years, Fenerbahce win a game against [an English side].

"Some people will remember but the number on the back of my shirt was 18 in Liverpool. So that's something really special for me in person.

"I said exactly the same thing to the players before the game. Although we are in a very difficult situation, we have a chance to bring another miracle in Istanbul. And if you get that miracle, things can change in a positive way."

They delivered in style, with 24-year-old former Derby County prospect Brown getting a goal and an assist in the second half.

"The Champions League is a great opportunity for Archie to show himself," said Kuyt.

"It's well known how good a player he is in Turkey. He did a fantastic job today. His defence and attack were very good. I'm very pleased with his performance, I'm pleased with the performance of all my players.

"It's a very special night for everyone who loves Fenerbahce."

#725. Here’s How the Midterm Elections Blue Wave Could Impact Music Policy in D.C.

With control of both the House and the Senate, Democrats will likely open new congressional investigations into the music industry — specifically, the live sector.

Democrats won a historic victory in the midterm elections on Tuesday (Nov. 3), flipping Congress and securing comfortable majorities in both the Senate and House of Representatives. The power shift is sure to affect policy across issues and industries, and music is no exception.

The chief area to watch come January will be congressional investigations and hearings — specifically, probes that dig into the live music sector. Democratic lawmakers are not happy with the eleventh-hour antitrust settlement reached between Live Nation and President Donald Trump’s Department of Justice (DOJ), and they’ll likely use their new gavels and subpoena powers to spotlight the president’s involvement in what they’ve called a “sweetheart deal.”

The DOJ settlement, inked one week into Live Nation’s antitrust trial, would require the company to cut back on some exclusivity practices but allow it to keep Ticketmaster. State attorneys general went forward with the trial and won a complete verdict on their monopoly claims. A judge is now weighing whether to adopt the settlement or grant the states’ much more drastic request for a forced Ticketmaster sale.

Democrats criticized Live Nation’s DOJ deal during a so-called “shadow hearing” in May, and Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), ranking member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, vowed to one day hold a proper hearing on the matter. “We will at some point, I guarantee, enter [your statements] into the record in full when we control committee hearings,” Blumenthal told witnesses, including California Attorney General Rob Bonta and indie promoter Jerry Mickelson.

Live Nation said in a Wednesday (Nov. 4) statement to Billboard, “The settlement provides meaningful, enforceable solutions, and we welcome the opportunity to answer questions about how it was reached as we focus on delivering on those commitments. The facts about what drives ticket prices haven’t changed, and we’ll continue working with policymakers on both sides of the aisle to address the issues that matter most to fans and artists.”

We can also expect a more robust congressional probe into ties between StubHub and Andro Capital, a ticket broker fund run by the company’s CEO Eric Baker. House Oversight Committee ranking member Rep. Robert Garcia (D-Calif.) opened an investigation in July after StubHub disclosed that Baker’s own fund had made more than $5 million in profits by reselling bulk ticket inventory on the platform since 2022.

Garcia has sought financial records detailing the relationship between StubHub and Andro, but up until now he has lacked the subpoena power to enforce those demands. That will now change in January. StubHub, for its part, has maintained that the Andro relationship is entirely aboveboard and “makes up only a small fraction of StubHub’s total revenue.”

“Eric’s investment in Andro Capital has been disclosed publicly,” said a StubHub spokesperson this summer. “Andro Capital is a separate company and is one of many vendors we use.”

One thing that likely won’t change after Tuesday’s Democratic victory is the music industry’s legislative agenda. That’s because music is a rare bipartisan issue in Congress. The two bills currently being most closely watched by the business, the American Music Fairness Act and NO FAKES Act, have support from both Democrats and Republicans.

Mitch Glazier, chairman/CEO of the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA), explained in an appearance on the Billboard On the Record podcast last month that the outcome of the midterms wouldn’t affect his current optimism about passing the NO FAKES Act, which aims to ban AI-powered voice cloning and deepfakes. “This is where we are so fortunate that our issues are completely bipartisan,” said Glazier. “It doesn’t matter if the House changes or the Senate changes, or they both stay the same, or they both change; this bill will be on a trajectory for quick introduction and quick movement.”

Glazier did, however, point out to Billboard On the Record that the music industry would lose one of its greatest advocates in Congress if Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.) succeeded in winning her state’s governor’s race. Blackburn indeed triumphed in Tennessee on Tuesday night, meaning she’ll no longer be around as a reliable sponsor of Senate bills that affect Nashville’s music scene. But Glazier highlighted some “rising champions” of music still in Congress, including Reps. Nathaniel Moran (R-Tex.), Becca Balint (D-Vt.) and Laura Friedman (D-Calif.).

#724. Serbia after Vucic: The winners are losing patience

After the Student List's election victory, Aleksandar Vucic's power apparatus is disintegrating. People want justice as soon as possible. But the losers still hold sway in the judiciary and administration.

Aleksandar Vucic is accustomed to the spotlight. As Serbia's all-powerful president, loyal media outlets followed his every move for years. His TikTok outbursts led the evening news. But on October 25 he lost the election to the Student List, and since then, a lot has changed.

Vucic complained at a press conference, before fewer microphones than usual, that the winners were practicing "revolutionary terror." He threatened: "If they continue to terrorize those who think differently – beatings, destruction and all the rest – and the state authorities do nothing, we will be forced to organize ourselves."

Vucic regards the immediate resignation of the general director of the Serbian state broadcaster RTS as an example of this "terror." Senior RTS editors have also been dismissed.

On Monday, a small group of protesters invaded the Informer TV station. Thousands of complaints have been lodged against Informer over the years for its demonization of Vucic critics. Now, journalists' associations are calling for its license to be revoked.

Tabloid media outlets loyal to Vucic have already changed their tone. Unlike Informer, they no longer refer to the Student List as "terrorists" and "mercenaries."

The List, which emerged from the student revolt, is made up of professors, activists and artists. In the election on October 25, it won 53% of the vote, leaving Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) trailing with just 39%.

Since then, things have moved fast. In many cities, citizens peacefully removed portraits of Vucic from municipal buildings. The public prosecutor's office for organized crime has launched investigations, including into electoral fraud. A special commission is examining the work of the Higher Public Prosecutor's Office in Belgrade, which critics say did Vucic's bidding, and persecuted his opponents.

The accusations against him are old ones: that he and his system kept the media under tight control; that state contracts were only awarded to companies loyal to the regime; and that Vucic, his party, and the Serbian state had links to organized crime.

The catalyst for the revolt was the collapse, two years ago, of the concrete canopy on the newly renovated railway station in Novi Sad. Sixteen people died. The accident is believed to have happened as a result of poor workmanship and corruption in the awarding and execution of the renovation contract.

Those who were celebrating in the streets a few days ago are already growing impatient. The new parliament has not yet been convened, and the SNS still controls many levers of power.

"A society that was oppressed for so long by a party that acted like a feudal lord now, understandably, expects justice," Dejan Bursac from the Institute for Philosophy and Social Theory at Belgrade University told DW. "In this power vacuum, people are getting impatient."

Vucic and leading officials promise to be a strong opposition and expect to make a quick comeback once "this lot" have ruined the country. But the majority of critics are calling for Vucic to be investigated and charged. "The SNS people are acting as if they had lost a local election somewhere in democratic Scandinavia, not as if they were part of a deeply corrupt and criminal regime," said Bursac.

It's very common in Serbia for politicians to switch allegiance from one camp to another. They go where the power is. Even Vucic has admitted that many of his former comrades-in-arms are turning their backs on him. "We are going to see cases of people resigning or staying in the shadows, even putting themselves forward as informants for the next government," said Zlatko Minic from Transparency Serbia, an organization that monitors the work of governments.

The million-dollar question is: How much damage can the old government do to the new one? "There's still time for many officials to award contracts and create financial obligations for the agencies they run without necessarily committing a criminal offense," Minic warned.

However, those familiar with the situation said that for some time now the Student List has had contacts with officials in the police and administration opposed to Vucic's style of government. The winners of the election may now be able to prevent certain actions. On Wednesday, the List again demanded the resignations of leading officials in the police and judiciary. Whistleblowers were also asked to come forward if the outgoing government should try to "destroy documents."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

In a symbolic move, Student List representatives held their first press conference in Pioneers Park in front of the parliament building. Vucic's followers fenced off the park in 2025, turning it into a pro-government encampment. According to investigative journalists, it also became a base for thugs and criminals who attacked anti-government demonstrators. The morning after the Student List's election win, its supporters went out with binbags and cleaned up the park.

The victorious Student List unites left- and right-wingers, pro-European and pro-Russian forces. It is focused on making changes in domestic politics and wants to advance European Union accession talks by implementing real reforms. The List opposes sanctions on Russia and the recognition of Kosovo — positions that almost the entire population of Serbia agrees with.

"Our plan is to stabilize and develop the country, not to destabilize it with some abrupt change of course on foreign policy," Oliver Toskovic, a psychology professor and future member of parliament, told DW.

Toskovic said that, unlike under Vucic, the EU will not be misused as a "cover." Serbia's EU accession process recently stalled, with Vucic accusing "the West" of inciting a "color revolution" in Serbia.

"We are very dependent on Russia for energy. This is really a mistake of the previous government," Toskovic said. "But for that reason, sanctions right now would destabilize the country. And that would not be good for us or for the EU." How energy policy will develop under a Student List government is still unclear.

Where Vucic would frequently take aim at Kosovo, Croatia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina, leading representatives of the new List have promised better relationships with Serbia's neighbors and a reduction in tensions. On Kosovo, Ilija Srdanovic, the Student List's lead candidate, has said the party is open to dialog with the government in the Kosovar capital, Pristina. He has already spoken by phone with the prime minister of Croatia.

The electoral process is not yet over. On Sunday, November 1, the vote will be repeated in some 50 polling stations because there were irregularities first time around. Once these votes are counted, parliament can be convened. The formation of a government is expected to be quick, but for now the names of the prospective members have not been disclosed.

#723. Cynthia Erivo Joins Snoop Dogg Biopic As This Key Character In Tupac Shakur’s Life

The Oscar nominee has added yet another film to her 2027 slate.

Cynthia Erivo has officially been cast as Tupac Shakur’s mother, the late former Black Panthers activist Afeni Shakur, in Universal Pictures’ upcoming Snoop Dogg biopic.

The three-time Oscar nominee and Tony, Grammy and Emmy winner joins a dazzling lineup that includes Jonathan Daviss as Snoop Dogg, Myles Bullcok Be as Dr. Dre, Lauren London as Beverly Tate and Camron Jones as Tupac. Snoop, which is currently in production in Southern California, is rounded out by Ice-T, Algee Smith, Tre Hale, Laya DeLeon Hayes, Olly Sholotan, Corey Champagne, Jonica Booth and SwayvoTwain. Explore 2Pac Cynthia Erivo Snoop Dogg See latest videos, charts and news

Afeni Shakur was a key figure in her son’s life. Tupac’s rocky relationship with her inspired “Dear Mama,” a Billboard Hot 100 top 10 hit (No. 9) that became one of the most beloved and acclaimed songs in the hip-hop canon. The single appeared on his 1995 Me Against the World LP, which earned a Grammy nomination for best rap album, while “Mama” snagged a nod for best rap solo performance. Erivo most recently graced the silver screen with this year’s Prima Facie, a legal drama that served as her official follow-up to her Oscar-nominated turn as Elphaba Thropp in 2024’s Wicked and 2025’s Wicked: For Good. Next year, Snoop expands her slate to four feature films, including animated musical fantasy comedy Bad Fairies, action thriller Karoshi and the highly anticipated fantasy film Children of Blood and Bone.

Hustle & Flow director Craig Brewer will direct Snoop, with Imagine Entertainment’s Brian Grazer — who helped bring Eminem’s 8 Mile to life — and Allan Mandelbaum joining on production. Snoop Dogg and Death Row Pictures president Sara Ramaker are also producing, with songs from the Cali rapper’s catalog set to appear in the film.

Erivo’s casting news comes amid a buzzy month for the multihyphenate. On Oct. 15, she played a solo headlining one-night-only show at the Hollywood Bowl, where she nailed covers of Barbra Streisand and Whitney Houston classics. Currently, Erivo is working on her turn as history-making South African singer Miriam Makeba in The Road Home, the forthcoming film from Dreamgirls director Bill Condon.

#722. The Tony Awards Renew With CBS Ahead of 80th Anniversary

The 80th Annual Tony Awards will broadcast live on CBS on Sunday, June 13, 2027.

The Tony Awards, which have aired on CBS continuously since 1978, are staying put, at least through 2032.

This makes the Tonys the most stable EGOT-level awards show in terms of its relationship with its broadcast partner. The Grammys, which aired on CBS from 1973 to 2026, are moving to ABC, Hulu and Disney+ beginning with the February 2027 show. The Primetime Emmys, which have aired on a rotation basis on Fox, ABC, CBS and NBC since 1995, are shifting to Prime Video in 2027. The Oscars, which have aired on ABC since 1976, will begin streaming on YouTube in 2029.

“We are thrilled to extend our long-standing partnership with CBS,” Heather Hitchens, president and CEO of the American Theatre Wing, and Jason Laks, president of The Broadway League, said in a joint statement. “For the past 48 years, we have collaborated with CBS to bring the best of Broadway to theatre fans all around the world and we look forward to marking the 80th anniversary of the Tony Awards with our best show yet.”

“CBS has a celebrated history of supporting the creative arts on television and the Tony Awards are a cornerstone of that past, present and future,” said Amy Reisenbach, president, CBS Entertainment. “George Cheeks and I are thrilled to extend the network’s 48-year partnership with the American Theatre Wing and The Broadway League and showcase the extraordinary talent, unforgettable performances and incomparable energy of Broadway to viewers across the country for years to come.”

The 80th Annual Tony Awards will broadcast live to both coasts on CBS and stream on Paramount+ (Premium) in the U.S. on Sunday, June 13, 2027.

Raj Kapoor, Sarah Levine Hall and Jack Sussman are set return to produce the 2027 Tony Awards. Kapoor and Levine Hall will serve as co-showrunners, while Patrick Menton and Rob Paine will co-executive produce, with Menton also serving as head of talent.

Kapoor is also an executive producer of the Grammys and the Oscars.

P!nk hosted the 2026 Tonys, becoming the biggest pop star ever to host Broadway’s Biggest Night. The Tonys have not yet announced who will host the 2027 show.

Schmigadoon! won best musical on the 2026 Tonys. Ragtime won best revival of a musical. The show also featured performances from three landmark musicals celebrating anniversaries: The Book of Mormon (15th), Rent (30th) and A Chorus Line (50th).

The LLRV was a bizarre, four-legged flying contraption commonly known as the "Flying Bedstead" used by Apollo astronauts for moon landing practice.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

On October 30, 1964, NASA's Lunar Landing Research Vehicle, or LLRV, took to the skies for the first time.

The LLRV was a bizarre, four-legged flying contraption commonly known as the "Flying Bedstead." NASA used it to simulate moon landings and liftoffs on Earth to prepare for Apollo 11, the first crewed lunar landing.

The first person to give it a whirl was the X-15 pilot Joe Walker. During this test flight, he reached an altitude of about 10 feet, and he hovered there for about a minute. He did this two more times that same day. In all, he completed more than 30 test flights with the LLRV.

These test flights took place at NASA's Dryden Flight Research Center in Edwards, California. That facility has since been renamed the Armstrong Flight Research Center after Neil Armstrong, who also piloted — and famously crashed — the "Flying Bedstead" before he went to the moon.

Over 60 years ago this LLRV test flight was a critical step toward landing humans on the moon for the first time, a historic moment that both served an important political purpose while also showcasing the result of monumental scientific and technical progress.

While images from this test flight might look like the team are having a bit of fun out in the desert, and perhaps they were, it was also deadly serious. The astronauts who signed onto these crewed missions were doing something that had never been attempted. They were putting their lives on the line for this progress, and this testing was a major piece in reassuring them and NASA that lunar landing could be accomplished, and safely.

Today, as we return humans to the moon with NASA's Artemis program, we see parallels between testing done over 60 years ago and testing today. Right now, SpaceX and Blue Origin are testing their lunar landers for crewed lunar landings in the near-future. While we have now been to the moon and have safely and successfully landed humans before, these tests remain critical for the safety and success of the missions.

Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.
